So many of the attacks on voting this year come down to Trump's ego. He'll never let himself believe he legitimately lost in 2020, and he is absolutely terrified of a Congress controlled by the same party he has labeled as "traitors" and so much worse.
He seems willing to do anything -- and we mean anything -- to suppress votes, kill mail-in ballots, and drive people away from the polls.
We're working nonstop to defend our fundamental right to vote from a hostile administration and opponents of voting rights around the country. RUSH $35 or more today to fuel that work and make every vote count in the midterms and beyond! >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=031526_2&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
Politico: Trump administration subpoenaing Arizona 2020 voting records, as Trump pushes to consolidate election power [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=031526_2&amount=25]
Team: The Trump administration has subpoenaed records related to the 2020 election in Maricopa County, which is Arizona's largest county.
The move comes just six weeks after the FBI raided an elections office outside Atlanta, seizing records related to the 2020 presidential election. This is because Trump and his cronies continue to spread debunked conspiracy theories about voter fraud in that election.
Arizona’s Maricopa County — like Georgia’s Fulton County — has long been a centerpiece of those conspiracy theories, with opponents of voting rights alleging widespread fraud in the 2020 election without evidence , even after multiple taxpayer-funded state investigations have found nothing.
Trump's MAGA DOJ is partly doing this to salve Trump's wounded ego over his 2020 loss. But they are also doing this to scare eligible voters away from participating in the crucial 2026 midterm elections.

Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes had a strong response:
“ What the Trump administration appears to be pursuing now is not a legitimate law enforcement inquiry ,” Mayes said. “ It is the weaponization of federal law enforcement in service of crackpots and lies. ”
The "why" is patently clear -- make as many threats as possible in purple states and key districts to scare off eligible voters and suppress them before they even try and take part in the ballot process.

Peter, I want to tell you something I don’t talk about much.
When you’re deployed to a combat zone, you get phone calls home. Not many. And they’re short. The connection is bad, the timing is worse, and you spend half the call pretending everything is fine so the people you love don’t worry.
**_My mom knew I wasn’t telling her the true situation._**
She knew that “I’m fine, mom” meant rockets had targeted the base that week. She knew that “it’s quiet here” meant I couldn’t tell her what was actually happening. And she knew that every time I said “I’ll be home soon,” there was a chance I wouldn’t be.
That’s the part of military service that doesn’t make the campaign ads.
We talk about the soldier. We don’t talk about the mom who can’t sleep. The dad who checks his phone every 30 minutes. The family who has to wonder if their loved ones will be home for Christmas this year.
My family lived that. For nine months while I was in Iraq, they carried the weight of not knowing if I’d make it home.
And they’re not special. They’re one of thousands of military families across this country who sacrifice in silence while politicians in Washington use the troops as props in photo ops and then forget they exist the second the cameras turn off.
I’m running for Congress because military families deserve more than a yellow ribbon magnet on someone’s bumper.
They deserve a representative who actually understands what it’s like. Who’s been on both sides of that phone call. Who knows that “supporting the troops” doesn’t mean clapping at an airport — it means fixing the VA, fighting for military spouse employment, making sure no veteran sleeps on a park bench, and making sure the men and women we send into harm’s way have a government that’s worthy of their sacrifice.
_**That’s what this campaign is about.**_
_**Not me. Not my Bronze Star. Not my resume.**_
_**The families.**_
Every mom who can’t sleep. Every kid who doesn’t understand why their parent is gone. Every veteran who comes home to a system that doesn’t care.
I’m fighting for them. And I’m asking you to fight with me. **Please, chip in whatever you can.**

subject: Halfway there

body:
Friend,
We’re officially halfway through the month, so we wanted to check in with you. Running a statewide campaign for Attorney General means building a team that can reach voters in every corner of Colorado – from the Western Slope to the Eastern Plains, and everywhere in between.
And right now, we’re in the middle of an important fundraising push to make sure we have the resources to keep growing this campaign.
Because the stakes couldn’t be higher.
Across the country, we’re seeing extremists attack voting rights, roll back environmental protections, and try to put themselves above the law. Colorado needs an Attorney General who will stand up to those attacks and protect our rights.
That’s exactly what I’ve done as Secretary of State – standing up to election deniers, defending democracy, and protecting Colorado voters. And it’s exactly what I will do as your next Attorney General.

EVERYONE SAW THE VIDEO.
**Earlier this month, GOP Senator Tim Sheehy got up from his seat at a Senate Armed Services hearing and physically assaulted a protestor.**
That protestor was Brian McGinnis – a U.S. Marine Corps veteran who was there to speak out against sending American troops into another war.
The entire thing was recorded. In the video, you can hear the snap.
**A sitting GOP U.S. Senator broke this veteran’s arm.**
And Sheehy’s response? He posted the video on social media. He called McGinnis “unhinged.” He said McGinnis was “looking for a confrontation.”
**No regret. No apology. Just pride.**
This Marine Corps veteran served his country. He showed up to exercise his right to protest. And he ended up in the hospital. _This is what happens when the GOP sends brawlers to the U.S. Senate instead of real public servants._

Federal officials say Jeffco violated Title IX. Here’s what happens next.
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**March 15, 2026** **SUNDAY NEWS DIGEST**
| | Dear Rocky Mountain Voice family,
Before we get into the news of the week, I want to invite you to check out the [latest episode of Unleashed](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)—and this one is especially important for Colorado’s business owners.
In this episode, I sit down with entrepreneur Joe Cherry to talk about how small businesses can push back against rising healthcare costs and government pressure while still taking care of their employees. Joe shares his remarkable story—from growing up in foster care to building a national company—and explains a new partnership that helps small businesses access better healthcare options while also [supporting Rocky Mountain Voice](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). If you own a business, or know someone who does, this conversation is worth a few minutes of your time.
Now to a story that absolutely exploded this week.
The federal government has ruled that [Jefferson County Public Schools violated Title IX](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), finding that the district allowed male students to access girls’ locker rooms, bathrooms, overnight accommodations, and sports teams—policies federal officials say denied female students equal protections under the law.
The investigation revealed that [61 roster spots on girls’ sports teams were occupied by male students](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) across the district, according to athletic records reviewed by federal investigators.
The Office for Civil Rights has now given Jeffco 10 days to comply—or face potential enforcement actions that could include the loss of federal funding.
Parents and watchdog groups say the ruling confirms what they’ve been warning about for years. The investigation was triggered by complaints from families and advocacy groups who raised concerns about safety, fairness in athletics, and policies that placed female students in private spaces with male students during school activities and overnight trips.
Under the federal directive, Jeffco must eliminate policies allowing males in female-only spaces, remove male athletes from girls’ teams, and publicly affirm biology-based definitions of male and female across district policies and athletic programs.
In other words: [federal law just overruled Colorado policy](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). And the stakes are high.
Jeffco serves more than 74,000 students and is already facing a $70 million budget deficit, meaning the threat of losing federal funding could force the district to act quickly.
It’s no surprise this story [lit up social media](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Hundreds of thousands of people have now seen the report—and for many parents, it raises a much bigger question: **who is protecting the rights of girls in Colorado schools?**
As always, we’ll continue following this story closely.
In truth & liberty, Team RMV

---
**[Colorado agriculture manager faces discipline after dispute over federal grant report and DEI training](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) A Colorado Department of Agriculture manager who challenged training language in a federally tied pest survey report now faces possible discipline after an internal investigation concluded he “more likely than not” misrepresented the document.
__
**[If you don’t defend it, you don’t own it: DeGette’s open border gamble](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY TOM ANTHONY, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) _The road to owning property resembles a superhighway to some and a Colorado jeep trail to others. To the Sioux it resembled a torn up mass of earth and buffalo chips; to the Comanche, four hooves and a mane._

**[Federal civil rights office finds Jeffco schools violated Title IX, gives district 10 days to comply](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) Girls in Jefferson County Public Schools have been sharing bathrooms, locker rooms, overnight accommodations and sports rosters with male students—and the federal government just said that has to stop.

|
---
**LEGISLATIVE SESSION**
_**Quick Summary of the Week:**_ _**In the Senate:** Senator Pelton’s _[SB-075](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)_ , which increases penalties for human traffickers, passed out of committee, while SB-097—a controversial proposal to _[decriminalize prostitution](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)_ —failed to advance. Lawmakers also approved _[HB-1001](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)_ , a Democrat-backed housing bill critics say weakens local control over development decisions. Meanwhile, senators passed a Women’s Day resolution, which sparked debate over language tied to _[gender definitions](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)_._
_**In the House:** House committees saw several contentious debates this week as Democrats used their majority to block a number of Republican-backed proposals. Bills addressing _[fairness in girls’ sports and extending malpractice timelines for gender-related treatments on minors](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)_ were both defeated in committee after testimony from doctors, athletes, and detransitioners. A separate measure that would have required abortion providers to _[offer adoption information to pregnant women](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)_ also failed to advance, while lawmakers continued debating energy policy proposals aimed at addressing _[rising electricity costs](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)_ and the growing role of _[state regulators in Colorado’s power grid](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)_._
_**Upcoming:** The Capitol calendar remains packed as lawmakers prepare to debate bills on taxes, housing, immigration enforcement, education funding, and energy mandates. Among the measures drawing attention are proposals affecting agricultural data ownership, clean fleet vehicle requirements, immigration-related training for law enforcement, and several health care and housing policies. Activists are also watching closely as multiple tax-related bills and proposals affecting TABOR refunds continue moving through the legislature._
|

**[Democrats Push Plan to Eliminate TABOR Refunds For The Next 10 Years](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**[COLORADO POLITICS](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) Colorado voters could decide this fall whether billions of dollars that would otherwise be returned as refunds under the Taxpayer’s Bill of Rights should instead go to public schools under a ballot measure unveiled Thursday by Democrats.

**[Colorado Democrat Shelves Prostitution Decriminalization Effort Amid Growing Criticism](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**[THE DAILY SIGNAL](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) Colorado’s Republican House leader is calling foul after a Colorado state senator says he is effectively killing his own bill to decriminalize prostitution—in order to protect “sex workers” from the trauma of having to testify.
__
**[All 66 Colorado Democrat Lawmakers Press Polis To Reject Clemency For Tina Peters](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**[THE COLORADO SUN](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) All 66 Democrats in the Colorado legislature signed onto a letter Wednesday urging Gov. Jared Polis not to reduce the prison sentence of former Mesa County Clerk Tina Peters, a missive that escalates the party’s near-universal disapproval of Polis’ posture toward the case.
_**[READ MORE ON LEGISLATIVE SESSION](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**_
|
---
**STATE**
**[Colorado Secretary Of State Jena Griswold Peddles Blatant Lie About Supreme Court Role](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**[TOWNHALL](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) This Democrat was caught spreading a complete lie, and it wasn’t difficult to expose. This political con job is occurring in Colorado, where Secretary of State Jena Griswold is running in the Democratic primary for the 2026 attorney general race.

**[Xcel Warns Grid May Need Coal Plants Longer Amid Delays In New Energy Projects](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**[THE COLORADO SUN](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) Xcel Energy, facing what it says is a shortfall in electricity generating capacity for the next two years, is proposing to run its four coal-fired units until 2030. Comanche Unit 2, in Pueblo, was supposed to close at the end of 2025. __
**[Before he was a congressional candidate, Manny Rutinel was calling animal agriculture “horrific”](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) Manny Rutinel spent the better part of six years calling animal agriculture a “horrific, exploitive industry.” Rutinel entered the legislature through an appointment in 2023 when Rep. Dafna Michaelson Jenet resigned from the District 32 seat. Less than two years later, he was filing paperwork for Congress.
**[READ MORE STATE NEWS](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**NATIONAL**
**[DOJ Review Finds Thousands Of Noncitizens On State Voter Rolls](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**[JUST THE NEWS](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) The top Justice Department prosecutor for civil liberties and voting rights tells Just the News that her ongoing review of state voter rolls has proven tens of thousands of noncitizens made it into a position to cast ballots and that hundreds of thousands of dead or departed residents were not properly removed from state election systems.

**[The SAVE Act’s strangest gift: it is making Democrats talk like noncitizen voting is real](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY C. J. GARBO, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) _For years, the Right has argued something simple: elections should be provably secure, not merely “trusted” by tradition, good intentions, or bureaucratic assurances. If only citizens may vote in federal elections, then citizen-only voting should be easy to verify, hard to fake, and consistently enforced._
__
**[Tracking the Iran conflict: A Colorado veteran’s daily sitrep from day 10 onward](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY KENNESAW, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) As a USAF ELINT veteran, I have always anchored my compass in Bible truth and the Founders’ original intent on liberty first, peace through strength, and no endless entanglements.

_**[READ MORE NATIONAL NEWS](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**_
|
---
**LOCAL**
**[When “blight” becomes a tool: How redevelopment labels unlock subsidies and eminent domain](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY CORY GAINES, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) _I had a friend (a Catholic) who once quipped that you can do anything you want in the Catholic church as long as you can find the right priest. I’ve thought about that quote in a variety of contexts because it’s pretty applicable. It certainly is in the Denverite article linked first below. That article details how the Denver Urban Renewal Authority (DURA) will be investigating the potential new location of the new Bronco’s stadium for evidence of blight._
**[High Winds Trigger Powerline Safety Measures in Boulder County](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**[DENVER7](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) High winds predicted for Thursday are prompting proactive measures by energy providers like Xcel. The company plans to implement an enhanced powerline safety setting — making lines more sensitive and automatically shut off power if something hits the line — on Thursday in several counties to allow power to remain in service with additional sensitivity protections in place. __
**_[READ MORE LOCAL NEWS](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)_**
|

**COMMENTARY**
**[HB 26-1246: Protecting Coloradans from rising power costs and a broken system](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY REP. KEN DEGRAAF, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) _Colorado is facing a turning point in energy policy. For years, families and businesses across our state have watched their electricity bills rise while our landscapes are increasingly carved up by massive transmission projects stretching from horizon to horizon. Forests, prairies, farms, and communities are being cut apart in the name of electrification and “grid modernization."_
__
**[The ROAD to Housing scarcity: Hidden provision in Senate housing bill may kill build-to-rent](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY BOOKER LIGHTMAN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) _You may have heard about a bipartisan omnibus bill currently being debated in the U.S. Senate, called the ROAD to Housing Act. From the name, you might think it’s about promoting housing construction, and that’s indeed how it’s being sold in the media._
__
**[Free to Choose Life](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY REP. SCOTT SLAUGH, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) _Upon arriving at the Colorado State Capitol in September to be sworn in as the new State Representative for District 64, I was eager to join the state lawmaking enterprise and already had a few ideas for new legislation. Soon I was advised by veteran lawmakers to reconsider my goals._

** Join me March 23 for a special event ‘Heroines of the Revolutionary War’ with Dr. Gloria Close
------------------------------------------------------------

Join us for a special women’s history month event supported by the Spartanburg Revolutionary War 250 Committee (https://www.spartanrevwar250.org/) on Monday, March 23 as we learn about Revolutionary Women of the Revolutionary War with Dr. Gloria Close. Dr. Close will share the stories of ten Heroines of the war who made a measurable impact. This event is free and open to the public with a reception to follow. Get tickets here. (https://www.eventbrite.com/e/heroines-of-the-revolutionary-war-featuring-dr-gloria-close-tickets-1984313117952?aff=oddtdtcreator)

In partnership with the Johnson Collection, guests will receive a private tour of the 25 for 25 collection at the Johnson Gallery (https://thejohnsoncollection.org/25-for-25/) beginning at 5pm, and we will move next door to Citizens and Southern for the program at 5:30pm. We will also be joined by Kimberly Wallner and Amanda Brinkley of the The Women’s Suffrage National Monument Foundation (https://womensmonument.org/) as they share exciting news about the first monument on the National Mall dedicated to Women’s History.

Questions? Email spartrevwar250@gmail.com.

** There will be a win in every run this year.
------------------------------------------------------------

As the Chair of the Spartanburg County Democratic Party, I’m thrilled to share that we will have a candidate competing in every state house seat in Spartanburg County in 2026. Spartanburg joins a handful of other counties across the state who have filled every seat, and we couldn’t be more proud. Filing opens March 16-30 and we’ll announce our incredible community members who believe in holding our elected officials accountable and fighting for something better at the state house, fighting for YOU.

And these candidates will play a critical role in mobilizing voters across the county to buoy our statewide races, races that could flip the Governor’s mansion and send Lindsey Graham into retirement. And it all starts in the Upstate.

Director's Report - Week 9 of the 2026 Legislative Session from the Desk of Nick Sotille SC House Democratic Caucus

At the end of each week during the 2026 Legislative Session, I will highlight what South Carolina House Democrats did at the State House. Here's what happened during the ninth week... But first, an important message about campaign season:

Candidate filing opens Monday! Are you thinking about running for office? Here's a pep talk from Rep. Gilda Cobb-Hunter: "Sign up. Join the fight. We'd love to have you," fighting alongside us in the State House. "Jump in, the water's fine!" (https://c8uafteab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001DWE1C6IpwrVGblVvJgq39QqHGeguXaY-PQQ7rDzA3B9X-1WZKcpIyVcUklUW3tw06Q5XU1DHZFF3-7zM9SbK5YBSwexzrSZ5biqBy3MTiqLoIjnl-I5iQ7NtliE3vVM7uFaHE97j420ajawi3Fyokq-BA5xpvXwMZXfVHLCNFH17e7YUl3psm6DVnJ1tVvMwjGO3Jkw5THa6SZsTBRVqpGtONkBQNLq7_PGefvaJAlGekHFyG4_EX6vhLcCNqG_dwy0VC-E2iPD2CeEzu73H5kzDBuOCKdU4Mgz5HnbqqAdQko0WiJCe94z1fk2SMxFKSKjHIAIno4Z28QKks9Wjfvk1tBcbWcom&c=yMSSiIzxWy1ihKBowaSSc9KPqB9XJ_Ixh1bkkej7vTZiQIxEGONu8w==&ch=A9kS4n291UP_NqgrZxaXxiQAbP1R0fsftVYDG69Zdwgas2G9vfyDyQ==) If you're thinking about it – or if you know someone who'd be a great candidate – then give me a call or text at 843-830-9405.

Defund Clemson? As soon as House Budget Week started on Monday, March 9, it went off the rails thanks to Republican extremists. These far right legislators hijacked the legislative process to score political points. Remember, they have a Republican Primary on June 9...

Republicans vote to raise taxes. Late Tuesday evening, Republicans in the South Carolina House of Representatives approved H. 4216 (https://c8uafteab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001DWE1C6IpwrVGblVvJgq39QqHGeguXaY-PQQ7rDzA3B9X-1WZKcpIyXGA8_l-qQFWU8kuZv1JfgYC7wzG6nYdMTiW3qGdUUs_T6FCPYJ5pyuXWrgclPuf2DqtQX6Px4tNMoL5wZmhZypNy7_CACxRcmxftcbHiFElgITDp02C1BezZ6kj_Br5V16NOsra4Lx45RaOHPAOQcZhd2DG3BFbSbbkYQB09Hz1s9plir7j_JFvc7cUwUMjMg==&c=yMSSiIzxWy1ihKBowaSSc9KPqB9XJ_Ixh1bkkej7vTZiQIxEGONu8w==&ch=A9kS4n291UP_NqgrZxaXxiQAbP1R0fsftVYDG69Zdwgas2G9vfyDyQ==) , a bill purported to lower state income tax rates – but it will actually raise taxes on many working people.

According to the bill's fiscal impact statement (https://c8uafteab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001DWE1C6IpwrVGblVvJgq39QqHGeguXaY-PQQ7rDzA3B9X-1WZKcpIyXGA8_l-qQFWv-tnr6eSVmp7d30ss7D7t-SQQ6MitmriViEldgDRhX4DgoXZeXJmASWc_nxDIEjHGJuldccUAVPvQm5vZAfaQywLrUvcTy0KqFw4kVWG-or0PXusSH8HnZA2QwXfhesbuDnvcqLkKk1XHO9QJghD1VL0wrs5hM3MJtCrfCwpKbb_UNzuTKaG18DS4S64HA499UpSD4CQnxY=&c=yMSSiIzxWy1ihKBowaSSc9KPqB9XJ_Ixh1bkkej7vTZiQIxEGONu8w==&ch=A9kS4n291UP_NqgrZxaXxiQAbP1R0fsftVYDG69Zdwgas2G9vfyDyQ==) , this legislation will have wildly different impacts on taxpayers at all income levels. For example:

• 32.4% of taxpayers earning between $20,001 and $30,000 will pay more.

• 30.5% of taxpayers earning between $100,001 and $150,000 will pay more.

• While 72.8% of taxpayers earning over $1,000,000 will pay less.

This bill will raise taxes on working people in order to give a tax cut to the wealthiest South Carolinians. While Democrats recognize the need to reform the tax code and lower the tax burden for all South Carolinians, we refuse to do that at the expense of middle class families.

The House voted to concur with the Senate amendments to the bill, so H. 4126 now goes to the governor to be signed into law. If you have any questions about the South Carolina House Democratic Caucus, please contact me directly at nick@schousedems.com (mailto:nick@schousedems.com) .

** Tell your Senator vote NO on the SAVE Act
------------------------------------------------------------

While Republicans have argued the SAVE Act is needed to safeguard elections, Democrats and voting rights advocates say the legislation would disenfranchise millions of Americans (https://spartanburgdemocrats.us15.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c155dbc88783023d5d7c3c7a9&id=067df9b5da&e=1508b56cd0) , including married women, by making it harder to register to vote and cast ballots.

This would mean that married women who have changed their surname would have to show citizenship documents that match their current legal name.

Because a passport or birth certificate may reflect a previous legal name, the legislation would add a new barrier to voter registration for those, such as many married women, who have changed their name, according to the League of Women Voters (https://spartanburgdemocrats.us15.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c155dbc88783023d5d7c3c7a9&id=18a06ca889&e=1508b56cd0) and Brennan Center for Justice. (https://spartanburgdemocrats.us15.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c155dbc88783023d5d7c3c7a9&id=d3ea268165&e=1508b56cd0)

Nine percent of Americans, or more than 21 million (https://spartanburgdemocrats.us15.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c155dbc88783023d5d7c3c7a9&id=523eb92f2b&e=1508b56cd0) people — including those who don't have a passport and those without (https://spartanburgdemocrats.us15.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c155dbc88783023d5d7c3c7a9&id=e44eafb225&e=1508b56cd0) a paper copy of their birth certificate — don't have those documents readily available, according to research from the Brennan Center for Justice. Read More. (https://spartanburgdemocrats.us15.list-manage.com/track/click?u=c155dbc88783023d5d7c3c7a9&id=af4f2841de&e=1508b56cd0)

An explainer on the SAVE Act (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=a38fx48Lf5E)

https://open.spotify.com/episode/6weXFBBZbMzKSEE6EqkirF?si=X46smqpwSUyBRG0-koh2oQ

This past week I attended an event for Sen John Ossoff and he reminded us that we have no choice but to win. We hosted our local party convention with more than a dozen candidates who’ve announced a run in 2026. This is an incredibly exciting election year in South Carolina.

I was honored to receive a Be HER Champion award at our local International Women’s Day event. And had a wonderful evening celebrating the ten year Anniversary of AFFA in Charleston last night.

Stay with me y’all, democracy is a participatory sport.

It wasn't easy telling the world I grew up dirt poor, I was raised by my Mamaw while my mother struggled with addiction.
It wasn't exactly the prep school/trust fund/summer-in-the-Hamptons upbringing that is commonplace in DC.
But I felt God called me to tell my story. Warts and all. I felt led to speak out because I believe millions of Americans share stories like mine. Stories of jobs being outsourced to China, addiction ravaging communities and killing our neighbors, and heeding the call of duty after the Towers fell on 9/11.
As your Vice President, I now stand in the breach for the left-behind, forgotten men and women who built this country, but were abandoned by the political class in DC.

name: Abdul El-Sayed
subject: I know how the system is rigged, and I know how to fight it
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Abdul for U
body:
[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/30?refcode=&t=1001&akid=1850%2E251025%2E0YYp_a ]Abdul for US Senate [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/30?refcode=&t=1002&akid=1850%2E251025%2E0YYp_a ]Abdul for US Senate

Hey Peter,

I'll be honest up front. I'm about to ask for your help. But before you
scroll past, I just ask for one minute of your time so I can explain why
this race matters so much.

Still with me? Thank you, genuinely. 🙏

I’ve been saying something for years that sometimes folks don’t
understand. It’s that Donald Trump isn’t the main cause of what’s wrong
with our politics; he’s just one of the loudest symptoms. The actual
disease is worse.

I know that can sound abstract, so let me make it concrete:

Trump didn't happen in a vacuum. He happened because for decades,
corporations and billionaires have been buying our politics — electing
politicians who serve them while leaving working people behind.

They rigged the healthcare system,
They rigged the tax code,
They rigged the trade deals,
And they made sure that the politicians who helped them rig it all got
rewarded handsomely for doing it.

Trump exploited that rot, and when he and his henchmen are gone —
eventually, they will be — the rot will still be there. The oligarchs will
still be there. The corporate PACs will still be there.

Unless we put people in the Senate who refuse to play that game.

That's why I'm running. I know how the system is rigged, and I know how to
fight it:

* We spearheaded a program to erase $700 million in medical debt for
300,000 Michiganders.
* We gave thousands of kids free glasses.
* We took on corporate polluters and won — and we did this all from a
locally elected office.

Just imagine what we could accomplish in the Senate,
Peter.

I wouldn’t only be Donald Trump’s worst nightmare. I’d be the worst
nightmare for any billionaire hoping to continue exploiting our politics
for their own financial gain.

Peter, I won’t
release a strongly-worded letter and call it a day. I’ll use every tool at
my disposal to fight for working people.

And here's the thing: Our campaign can actually win. Depending on the
poll, we're in first or second place in this primary. This is not a
long-shot campaign. It's a campaign that needs resources to go the
distance.

So today, I'm asking for your help. Together, we’ll win this competitive
election and send a message that the era of bought-and-paid-for politics
is over.

Not everyone can give the same amount — and that’s the beauty of a
people-powered campaign. Some will step up with larger gifts, others with
smaller ones. Together, we build something stronger than corporate PACs
ever could.

* If you have done well and can afford it, please consider giving a bit
more for those who can’t. [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1166?amount=10&refcode=em20260315-1840&t=1004&akid=1850%2E251025%2E0YYp_a ]Click to donate $1,000, $500, $100, or as
much as you can.
* If you can give at the grassroots level, [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1172?c0=em-ms-aes-20260315-1-ak.-ntyWM&refcode=em20260315-1840&t=1005&akid=1850%2E251025%2E0YYp_a ]chip in $25 or whatever
you're comfortable with.
* If you can't give right now, that's okay too. Share this email.
[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/843?utm_source=em20260315-1840&t=1006&akid=1850%2E251025%2E0YYp_a ]Volunteer. Spread the word. Your support is just as essential to
this movement as any donation.

I know this email was long. I hope it was worth your time.

We have work to do, but we can win.

Your friend in the fight,

Abdul

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Emails like this help us stay connected with grassroots supporters like you, so thank you for taking the time to read this message. To contribute via check, please address it to Abdul for U.S. Senate, PO Box 126, St. Clair Shores, MI 48080.

Receive Fewer Emails: https://act.abdulformichigan.com/signup/receive-fewer-emails/?t=1007&akid=1850%2E251025%2E0YYp_a

Email us: info@abdulformichigan.com

You might’ve heard us say it before, but it’s still true!
If Democrats are going to take back the U.S. House, the path runs straight through California.
Right now there are six key districts we need to secure a Democratic House majority. Thanks to Proposition 50, several of these districts now lean in our direction — but only if we organize and win them.
That’s why the California Democratic Party is already building organizing programs in these battleground districts.

name: Jon Bonck For Congress
subject: Former TX38 Candidate Michael Pratt endorses Jon Bonck
body:
| | | | |
---
| FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE Date: March 16, 2026 Contact: william@jonbonck.com
Michael Pratt Endorses Jon Bonck for Congress in TX-38 HOUSTON, TX -- Tomball ISD Trustee, U.S. Marine Corps veteran and former congressional candidate Michael Pratt has endorsed Jon Bonck for Congress in Texas' 38th Congressional District, adding his support to Bonck's growing coalition of conservatives across the district.
Pratt, who ran in the Republican primary on March 3rd, and had a strong grassroots campaign focused on conservative leadership, service, and results, said he is supporting Bonck as the race continues and Republicans focus on the future of the district.
"I'm incredibly grateful to the thousands of voters, volunteers, and supporters who believed in our campaign," said Michael Pratt. "My commitment to serving this community continues, and I intend to serve in public office again. Service has always guided my work, and I will continue working with conservatives across TX-38 to strengthen our community and advance the principles that brought so many people together during this campaign. As the TX-38 race moves into the runoff, I'm proud to support Jon Bonck and wish him success."
Pratt currently serves on the Tomball Independent School District Board of Trustees, where he has advocated for students, parents, and strong neighborhood schools. During his campaign for Congress, Pratt emphasized his conservative results and advocacy for conservative principles including limited government, fiscal responsibility, and protecting Texas values.
Bonck thanked Pratt for his endorsement and for the campaign he ran during the primary.
"I appreciate Michael's support and the effort he put into this race," said Jon Bonck. "Running for Congress takes a great deal of commitment and sacrifice for candidates and their families. Michael ran a great campaign and has served the Tomball community incredibly well through his work on the Tomball ISD Board of Trustees. I'm grateful for his endorsement and look forward to working with him not only on the campaign trail, but in Congress as well" Bonck said his campaign will remain focused on the issues that matter most to the people of Texas' 38th Congressional District, including lowering costs for families, restoring American energy dominance, and defending conservative values in Washington.
Bonck has been endorsed by President Donald Trump, U.S. Senator Ted Cruz, Harris County Commissioner Tom Ramsey, Congressman Jim Jordan, Congressman Brandon Gill, Congressman Tim Burchett, and many other conservative leaders.

## $10B TikTok Fee for White House
The Trump administration is set to [collect roughly $10 billion](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL-umzAchZ_GbI6MARMGhlQV2-3S4aoTMvYh_Br_QbYTlD59RfsIdz2f9Enn-_yYPzQ5Cvcf2mMsa5wDjuxQCtJci6XQo8THCnidzOa1DchZz1JIxUXDazVbTe49t5UdV0CiqTDWfd-orlNDX23jIHFdMJhW9ULqVctB2Vaaazeo9gqrKhpPm2hqVQtxrbsLRLc05uTopdADawUslZguvyOFsmF17_hCupjoKzdupeyZNTcmJyan4zguPoeTMTkh8GdmcvIx4M3kZKLfdSCcW0lPv3NtPQXKJelCMfCMwkvkCQb0Aq8FX8i5k6wAX2PiS4oPJAp3_r8Nt9COyUknfrvVv_586idrpmjIsub7t7MsjvwTaa_SaPfjtGXVs1bcvSb370P5UvjXKP8GAAD__2FbmNk) from investors who took control of TikTok's U.S. operations, according to reports, a near-unprecedented fee for a government's role in brokering a private deal. Oracle, Silver Lake, and Abu Dhabi investor MGX paid the Treasury about [$2.5 billion](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFytCAYRZ9GOxz4FFgLir_Zbv82pYNyXcmCOEh09u0zJo-Q_sy9c87HY3hYH_z6_G8jTJnTsOLcA0pBHgQfi3-V9JqBaPO0ROtW7LsdiJNivGVCDc768B662pkZILQ1jNC6VVKqXteLISkdcdf1k6ObHp0GblaS63qBqZeovbnWeCuU4PwmZAMux3aSveqgidu-6jicLyk3n8mvZcEc3ulAbqYU62CWUra9av9VdK_ofp5ncymcwOsCKrqX_BU3Zl30KyuJZUzwB5jgbPQh-LSyOafIflWZgw0sY0u5MCGU1oqozsZt5wXvSlcdf0brw899-VOzw9B3AAAA__-XAYAi) at the deal's close in January, with additional payments scheduled to continue until the total reaches $10 billion. Vice President JD Vance has said the new U.S. entity is valued at about $14 billion, a figure some analysts say [dramatically undervalues the platform](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO4yAURb8Gd1iPhwFTUGzjLttuaWHziNlgiGwmUf5-5PmFqe_VvTrn322--ZRTuf_1O7kW61zofWZqjY5ZwNLSo9VHJNr9sW67D4XO088IqDlILvQcfMqfeeiCi0RIsiMnjJFaKW1Nt7loAQJYIbUNMnq1yGgXYcw4EgYxxi65aw2k0AJgFKonUItcldUDGQRv2QAUUqtH_7-m0jaK-VNfdPRr3bvsttaeJ5N_GE4Mp5iKLyv1H7_VejUYThcSw-nr5AetlF7EBfAl5Zxq4ZGII6IFhVb0W9tzd7jwfF_xqQ0b4L77lH_O2q8MvRx-BwAA__-jf3fu) and its 170 million American users. The deal adds to a growing list of administration moves extracting value from the private sector, including a 10% stake in Intel and a cut of Nvidia chip sales to China.
## Iran Rejects Talks with US
President Trump said Saturday that Iran wanted to make a deal but that [the terms weren't good enough](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2O3CAURp8Gd4wwNpApKCZK3O02KaJU1l24HrPLj3NhFs3bR84rbH2kT985v1_WFwgx5PsrJLRtK2vGXiO2hrSO4q2Fj1Y-NsQE5PYEPmOtsEohNRcTH_XqIcTnOg_ebogSpwHtaMykldJXM-xWg9dX5cym1eacHMW8IcyAs_DCKGOGYM81MY16FOLbqC4o1Nvk1FXPaKSAK5sF-tAKXd5LyG3HLT7LJ9LFlTREu7d2VDbdmFyYXHrvl1TzyZhcMPNHZXI5pU5YKHoml0aPdHDCd3Stco8QeQ9t54Eg85K5exBhbrwhpcqh8g7ECe5YeclMLkD8dhv__Pz7emPTUlzwbPrx_ayIvf5COgay_ughxlC1YbO4Jwjx_9_2pcifVv4LAAD__4IgkRs), demanding Tehran abandon its nuclear ambitions and adding that he's hearing the new supreme leader may "not be alive." Iran's foreign minister fired back Sunday, saying Tehran has [never asked for a ceasefire](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LtuwyAYxfGnwVss7uCBoYu3dO2IuHzExNhENgrK21fuK3Q-0k86_5-7vbtc8v74dhuYlqrdoZ8FWoPDEuxbXltdE8DmjrBsLu5wns5STOUNsxuRNrpcPpYP0SQACmwAQ5RiUgg5qWExjgunQQUfdRIadPRpShMDJyXwENmQzaVhRiTBWBMxAhaeBTFJDopiNyGOIeZWj_FZ894WSOVT33CMoW5DMUtrrxOxL0RnROfe--h9uDZE5-sMonPJb0B0DuuDdPJ86fXZhsPEV8-l5FMqxPFjc7n8ie1fGd6G_gYAAP__uWhwjg) and insisting the new leader is in "good health," though he has yet to appear publicly. Israel said it struck more than [200 targets across Iran](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLtuwyAUhp8GNltcDMQDQxdv6drROjaH-DTYRIBi5e2r5BW6_xd93891vgIlOm7fsKNvMc8HnjVha1hmKZZG95bvEXGHsm47hANrhVkJZTuhO2nnAJRe88CDj4gKNUcvndPWGDs6vvnR2WCjxKiGxSFYG5bLCisYPdpBXgQn_14TWlopxEWaHoVZ9GpGO6BTAkY2CAzUcul_Mx1tw5he-YmlX_POk99ae1Smv5iamJrO8-wb7VhzpFoA0zvF1JToiUvKt-4D0knTvV-Zmnjx4XFSSlStY4O47UCfEm__8vH06i8AAP__Fxlysg) on Sunday alone, expanding operations into western and central Iran, while Gulf states reported fresh waves of Iranian drone and missile attacks. Germany became the first major ally to [publicly decline Trump's call](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2SozAUBODTQCZK6A8TKNiEzJtuSMnoAW-tH5f0bIo5_ZRdc4M5QH_d1f-u89VhwLT9dREsrXlOcNQARFDmnt8I75TvK0B0Zdmj8wlqdbPgwjAuWW9m7zCcs2q9XQEEyBZsPwzSaG3God0tH6WXnmsPXIrVmN47JfWotbrI1SjVon1rXPam5_zS6w64vslFj0bBILgbG8XBI-XS_c-YaIc1nPkFpVtybIPdiR61kX8aMTViOo6ji-h9AHCVYk6f4JJjI6afHs02KNGlk5VngMryk9hbxrQxTAQlOcKcXGARA5IrJ4tYK-bEKLNHyQQLsUrFIbG8sj2X-PxqxNQW6x8HhoDVDI3iW3QYPivpV9e-rPgOAAD__xgPjz0) for warships in the Strait of Hormuz, though South Korea, Britain, and Japan said they were reviewing the request.
## March Madness Bracket Drops
The NCAA March Madness bracket was released last night, giving college basketball fans their first look at the 68-team field. Duke, Arizona, Michigan, and Florida earned No. 1 seeds, though that hardly guarantees anything in a tournament defined by pure chaos. [See the bracket here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2O6yAUxfHV4M7WBWwwBcVr3OW1UyI-LjETbCKMbGX3o0Szg6mP9NdP5-tmbjbltN__2w11i8XseB0ZW8NqKLiWHq08IuJmq183G3Y8DmsYMNED76kwwab8MmMXdERkyDvUVEoupkko2a2aesVRjPMcHQUlVaRSoAfH5YwuqKlL-l0DTgUFmOk0IEyO-0mJESUDq8gIGFIrdfguaW8rxvwqJ9bBl63Lem3teRD-j7CFsOW6rmH31r5HwpYPu_919zmdSNjiqvUPbF3V4XmlnNMhJBnhvtmUP9H2pydOzX4CAAD__1tscUE). It's hard to predict where upsets will happen. Popular [bracket busters](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGy4yAMRb8Gd2RAjsEuXGxD97bd0iOD8sIGgweUePL3O87sH7xKhTRH99w_X8sXxhTz92_caOZbWTIdLREz1UWrleODy-NGtGH19w1DptZwAQVGql5qswSM6b1cuzDfiID6jmZtbW-GwUy2u8-WJt9bg0PQ67AG48dp1BZWrWwIFtcuzidN9dpopUY9XEgNa--HyVzJgsJJXBWFyKVe_paY-U639C4vqhdfti7Nd-a9if6XACfAHcdxeTbkEvB9HghwjUt9n3MvlZsAlz3iKsBxedZM5-pMIMCpXoDTgwD30ZX_feVzb8Ryj_7R5F4pRM-x5CZPkPxQcKPMcq3oH8TSxxyoUkp4vhsnDWoarVJWgOvqHPYjphSbseKqvjeM6aPCP-r_NcO_AAAA__9Vj5jO) include High Point, the historically feisty VCU Rams, and a scorching-hot Miami (Ohio) squad that has lost just one game this season. The East region is one of the best we've seen in years. No. 1 Duke will have to navigate a [gauntlet](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGypCAQBdCvwaynEBU0MNjE7G26odUDjbCDYEnPs97fbzm_sHFXn3vr_vlavzCmmLffuNPMvqyZrpqImc61lU-OLy4vT7TjacOOLlOtuCqpNMgOWr06jOln7Rs3eyJFXUNza0ynh0FPpglzZ_XkvB69HT3R5KXuW6W8kaM3ZvSmifOtya7VrZRjOzxIDs_ODpPuySiJk-glucjlfPwtMXMgn37KN50PW_YmzYH5qKL7JdQi1HJxOe6DUEu2iPDE-iJ-YkpCLXeQUIvshFq4HHArmBJUIgfu_SLYiCsgcHlvAT4AYWU4aYslgzvxgitygLctOUO4n4sHjzuBLWgDVaGW5pzdccWUYtVG9HLbMaZPW_6vib9n9S8AAP__we2P9Q) that includes No. 2 UConn, No. 3 Michigan State, No. 4 Kansas, and No. 5 St. John's--all legitimate Final Four contenders. name: Ernest Lineberger
subject: I stand relieved – having passed the torch of flipping Texas CD26 ​
body:
[image: image.png]

This is a special, personal email to friends and donors from Ernest
Lineberger.
It’s long, but meaningful to me.

When in the course of military timetables, it comes time for one officer to
take over certain responsibilities from another, when the oncoming officer
is ready, he/she states “I relieve you, sir”. The off-going officer
replies “I stand relieved”. By this formality, there is no confusion about
which officer is responsible.

In my naval career, I changed jobs / duty stations multiple times. The
navy is a very dynamic organization with people rotating in and out of
shipboard assignments so regularly that ‘hail and farewell’ events were
often held monthly. And while in an assignment, you are normally on a
watch cycle where you rotate in and out of the immediate urgent duties of
watch standing for various purposes of ship safety and operations. These
are normally laid out in a timetable (watch bill) and well understood by
all involved. Seldom are two individuals vying to stand the same watch.

At the beginning of this campaign journey, it seemed like I was being
called to an impossible task, flipping a seat in the US House of
Representatives that had been Republican for forty years. Somehow, I grew
into it and saw an opportunity to serve my community, the nation and the
world. Winning and flipping this seat was always a long shot, but the
possibility for success continues to improve. The initial mission
objective was simple enough. Get on the ballot as a Democratic Candidate
for US House of Representatives for Texas congressional district 26 for the
2024 election. The point being that there had been no such candidate in
2022 and all indications were that there would be none in 2024.

My 2024 primary was uncontested. In fact, there were other congressional
districts that still did not have a Democratic candidate. I poured my
soul, my time, my money, my family and friends into the race for the 2024
general election. I won endorsements and learned a lot with the
experience. The 2024 loss was painful. It wasn’t close. But we had
started something. We had a foothold and had begun growing a groundswell
of support. More and more people came out with curiosity and interest. I
was convinced that building on what we had would be so much stronger than
someone else starting new, or worse no one again in 2026. Plus, instead of
one year, I would have two full years to grow my campaign, my name
recognition and share my message throughout the district.

So, I kept the watch. I stayed on duty and on station. I patrolled my
district regularly making appearances in Cooke, Wise and Denton Counties.
You could see and feel the support and appreciation for my efforts to feed
in to the Democratic effort, the county parties, the Democratic clubs, the
candidates for other offices in and around CD26. It was so good to see
2026 developing as a very strong year for Democrats. The Republican
administration was creating chaos with extreme cruelty and no signs of
compassion while spreading corruption with no concern for any of the
potential consequences for anyone. While the Democrats fielded a full team
of qualified, empathetic and intelligent statesmen and women who would
fight to take over proper stewardship of the state’s and nation’s resources
for the good of the people. I was proud and honored to be one of them.

But make a plan and be ready to hear God laugh. On Tuesday, March 3, 2026
with the primary election, my tour of duty as Democratic Candidate for a
seat in the US House of Representatives came to an end. With these
results, that responsibility falls to my primary opponent, Steven Shook.
And I wish him well. The gains achieved and challenges remaining are now
fully his to use and leverage toward mission success.

Fortunately, I’m not entirely unprepared for my next assignment. Now,
retired from a naval career as well as a second career in semiconductor
manufacturing, my success in a future role as fully retired grandpa is
nearly assured.

With that long preamble, many, many thanks and accolades of appreciation
must go out to so many who jumped in with support of all kinds to help me
in this role as candidate. Grassroots financial support from over 2,400
individuals totaling over $186,000 in amounts from $1 to $6525 helped power
the campaign with supplies, advertising, overhead and more. Volunteers
made that campaign possible on such a small budget, donating their time
and talent to bring our message deep in the district. The energy is
contagious. These investments of time and trust deserve a good outcome. I
regret that I will not be the one to see the mission through to
completion. That I will not be able to look each of my volunteers,
supporters and donors directly in the eye as I’m sworn in to office to
serve the people and say to each one “You made this happen!”. I know that
I’m not letting them down. As a former track team member, I’m simply
passing the baton. With their support, I ran my part of the race. We
helped close the gap.

Emotions run strong. Some disappointment. Some relief. Some guilt. Some
failure. A mix of feelings that I failed to get to office to see through
the good that I would do for my community and the nation. And yet, so many
have reached out with words of encouragement and appreciation for my effort
and team building. The concern they share for my well-being over their own
sense of disorientation from the change is more encouraging.

I’m using the closing days of my campaign committee to do what I can to
support some other great candidates. Here are two wonderful servant
leaders that can use your support, a donation of any amount, to help them
clear the hurdle of their run off elections and on to win their general
election against MAGA incumbents.

Vikki Goodwin for Lt. Governor will ultimately challenge Dan Patrick for
this key Texas office that controls the Texas Senate and the bills that
come up for a vote there. Vikki is a four term Texas Representative who
well understands the workings of Texas government. I’ve been supporting
her statewide campaign with her top priorities of housing, education, water
and healthcare. If you can volunteer to help out the campaign, please visit
her "Get Involved" page <https://www.vikkigoodwin.com/getinvolved>
<https://www.vikkigoodwin.com/getinvolved>on the web to sign up. Also, if
you're able to chip in to help fund the fight, you can find that form here
<https://secure.ngpvan.com/HXtX4Rvv4E-3N3V6P-qnoA2>. Vikki needs your help
to lock in her place. You can learn more at www.GoodWin4Texas.com
<http://www.goodwin4texas.com/>.

Kevin Burge for US House (Texas CD24, just South of my district) will
ultimately challenge Beth Van Dyne and help flip the House majority
Democratic to regain control of Congress and reign in the executive
overreach of tariffs, wars, tax breaks for billionaires, and more. This
marine veteran is exactly who we need to restore stewardship of our
national policies. You can learn more about him, his campaign, and donate
to support him through a successful runoff election at Kevin Burge for
Congress <https://www.burgeforcongress.com/>.

For those who made it this far in a long email, I salute you and appreciate
your fortitude. I will be closing down my campaign committee soon, but
still doing what I can to see these and other candidates successful in
their campaigns. If you want to help me with final bills, you can still do
so for a short time by donating through LinebergerforUScongress.com
<https://www.linebergerforuscongress.com/>

One Community – Diverse But Not Divided.

Putting People’s Needs First!

Your friend and neighbor,

Ernest Lineberger

## New Statue of Kipper Mease Unveiled
Family members of the late Roy "Kipper" Mease gathered at the Pasadena sports complex named in his honor last week for the unveiling of a [new bronze statue](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO4yAQhp8Gd0QMJMYpKK6h22uvtCYwiVEwWDCJd9_-5Dud7gG2HX2aX9_362P-wJRTefzElRx_3utcaO-ZmKnNnZFf1GjLGCiu2MKyYizUZ630KJWRMM4RU_6az0N0NxWvMJADa814ma4wDYtTgc5h0hYR7niJN4sAkzG3ADeyKsCQ3PFMGRgBFFzsCRRQDBMYbacLTVdxVhQT13bihZg-sd_zV31TO4W6DtktzFsX5ofQXmi_7_sp5BSeeqmvzrUclND-0BLa5xowC-2PTaG9MkJ7UEL7JAtRlFxlTm-SuZaHpFJfj-W4dSKZWP5LITvXTEU-07ZRkythJ_m31n8GWW7YMVJBuWF7Cu2H5uK2p5xTH604q8eKKf_R4O_Ffzv9OwAA__8sdppl) to replace one that was stolen in December 2024. Everyone in politics is asking the same question right now: why are Democrats losing young men? More specifically, why are so many young men gravitating toward what people call the "manosphere"--the online ecosystem of influencers, podcasts, and personalities built around hyper-masculine identity, grievance politics, and reactionary culture.
A lot of people try to explain this through economics. They say young men feel left behind financially, that wages are stagnant, that housing is unaffordable, and that stable careers are harder to find. All of that is true. But I think the deeper issue is something more psychological. It is about the perceived opportunity to be successful in this country: successful financially, successful as someone who can take care of a family, and successful in terms of status and identity--strong instead of weak, respected instead of emasculated.
At its core, this whole dynamic is about belonging to the pack. The manosphere has become very good at reinforcing that pack mentality, tapping directly into one of the most primal fears young men have: the fear that if you fall behind, you will be left behind. Thrown out in the cold. Left out of the tribe.
For years Democrats have talked about leveling the playing field and expanding rights. Those are good goals and necessary ones. But while we were doing that, the Right--and an entire ecosystem of influencers--were telling young men a very different story. They told them something simple: that they are losing something before they ever even had the chance to have it. When you frame the world that way, it feels deeply unfair. The story these men hear over and over again is that society is designed to make sure they never succeed, and worse, that they will be left behind.
## **The Theology of Dominance**
One of the ways these insecurities get reinforced is through religion. Over the past several decades, a particular strain of Christianity has become very influential in American politics, especially through the rise of the Evangelical Right, Christian Nationalism, and the Prosperity Gospel. Figures like Jerry Falwell and Pat Robertson helped popularize a worldview where masculinity is not simply natural but divinely ordained dominance.
Men are told they are supposed to lead, supposed to dominate, supposed to control. If that hierarchy is challenged, it is framed not merely as social change but as an attack on God's design. And once you frame it that way, it becomes extremely difficult to argue against. After all, how do you argue with God?
This is not the same set of Christian values emphasized in many other traditions. In Catholic, Methodist, and Episcopal communities, the emphasis is often placed on service, humility, and dignity for all people. But the version amplified in political media often sounds very different: God blessed me by letting me be born in the United States, and I have the freedom to do whatever I can to make it. Success becomes proof of righteousness. Power becomes proof of virtue. Hierarchy becomes holy.
## **The Fear of Replacement**
Most of these men do not hate women. Many of them want the same things previous generations of men wanted: relationships, families, stability, and the sense that hard work will lead somewhere. But they are also being told that as women gain opportunities and advance professionally, their own chances at achieving those same dreams are shrinking. They fear they will be forced to step aside. They fear they will be replaced.
For decades, young men were raised with a fairly clear expectation of adulthood: work hard, earn a decent wage, support a family, and society will recognize your role as a provider. But the economic system that supported that model has been eroding for years. Wages have stagnated, housing costs have exploded, and stable careers are harder to find. The path to adulthood now feels far less certain than it did for their parents.
Into that uncertainty, right-wing media offers a very convenient explanation. You are not struggling because the system changed. You are struggling because someone else took your place.
Take the panic around the term DEI. Why does it scare so many men? Because they are told that DEI is not about expanding opportunity but about demoting them. The argument they hear constantly is simple: those opportunities have to come from somewhere, so they must be taken from you. In that narrative, every promotion given to a woman becomes proof that men are being pushed out, every scholarship aimed at historically excluded communities becomes evidence that the system is rigged, and every diversity initiative becomes another symbol of their supposed decline.
Emotionally, that translates into something very tangible: less money, less opportunity, less respect, and less likelihood of building a stable life. Perhaps most powerful of all is the fear of looking like a failure. For generations, masculinity has been tied to the ability to provide. When that role feels threatened, the fear becomes existential. If they cannot fulfill the version of manhood they were raised to expect, then who exactly are they supposed to be?
The Right does not try to resolve that anxiety. It weaponizes it. Young men are told something simple: you did not fall behind, you were pushed, and someone else took what should have been yours.
## **The Scarcity Mindset**
The same psychological dynamic appears in immigration debates. If you asked most of these young men for a detailed policy solution to immigration, they probably would not have one. They are not thinking about visa systems, asylum law, or labor markets. What they are reacting to is something much older: the belief that someone unknown is coming to take what belongs to them.
Whenever people believe resources are limited, the instinct to guard what you have becomes powerful. Immigration is often framed through that lens. The emotional reaction is not really about the jobs immigrants take, but about what those jobs represent.
Their own families may have taken those same jobs generations ago, but history rarely feels relevant in moments of insecurity. What matters is perception. And the emotional logic becomes very simple: so what? It is mine now. If someone else gets it, that means I lost.
That kind of thinking turns opportunity into a zero-sum game. If someone else rises, it must mean you are falling. The Right has spent years reinforcing that narrative. Immigration becomes not a complex policy issue but a direct threat to personal stability and identity.
## **Masculinity and the Culture War**
The same insecurity helps explain the intensity of today's culture wars. Why do some men react so strongly to being called "gay" or "weak"? Why does the existence of trans people provoke such visceral reactions from people who insist it has nothing to do with them?
For many of these men, the answer comes down to hierarchy. They were raised with a model of masculinity that works like a ranking system. At the top sits the ideal man: strong, successful, emotionally unshakeable, and clearly in control. Everything else sits somewhere below that standard.
When cultural norms shift and those boundaries blur, it can feel like the structure itself is under attack. Being called weak is not simply an insult; it is an accusation that someone has fallen down the social ladder. Once someone believes their identity is under threat, the conversation stops being about policy or social norms and becomes about survival.
## **The Influencer Pipeline**
This is where the internet becomes incredibly powerful. When young boys say something ignorant or make a bad joke--as kids often do--the reaction they receive can shape how they interpret the culture around them. Sometimes that reaction is constructive. But online, it is often immediate condemnation.
For a teenager trying to figure out where he fits in the world, that can feel less like correction and more like rejection. That moment of friction is exactly where the influencer pipeline begins. Right-wing content creators are extremely good at identifying that feeling and exploiting it. They step in and say: they hate you, but we don't.
Suddenly someone who felt embarrassed or rejected finds an entire online culture celebrating the exact behavior he was criticized for. What was once criticism becomes validation. What was once embarrassment becomes identity.
Over time, podcasts, livestreams, and social media personalities build an ecosystem where exaggerated masculinity becomes entertainment. At first it is framed as comedy--just jokes, just guys being guys. But gradually humor turns into grievance, grievance turns into ideology, and the algorithm rewards whoever pushes the boundary further.
Eventually defensiveness hardens into identity.
## **The Political Validation**
Eventually those cultural frustrations move into politics. That is where someone like Donald Trump enters the picture. For many young men already immersed in this ecosystem, Trump does not just look like a political candidate. He looks like validation.
He says the same things they have been hearing for years: that elites are mocking them, immigrants are taking their jobs, the system is rigged, and masculinity is under attack. The message resonates not because it is sophisticated but because it feels familiar.
Trump reinforces the deeper worldview at the center of the movement: that life is a competition between winners and losers. Strength is everything. Weakness deserves ridicule. Success is not something shared; it is something conquered.
Supporting him becomes less about policy and more about recognition. He speaks their language. He validates their frustration. He gives their insecurity a political home.
## **Where We Went Wrong**
So where did we go wrong? The answer is complicated. Many of the social changes that expanded opportunity were necessary and long overdue. But somewhere along the line, our cultural conversation about masculinity shifted in a way that many young men interpreted as rejection rather than reform.
Instead of saying masculinity should evolve, the conversation sometimes sounded like masculinity itself was the problem. The difference between toxic masculinity and masculinity itself became blurred. What many young men heard was not "be better," but "be less"--less aggressive, less competitive, less masculine.
When identity feels attacked, people rarely respond by embracing criticism. They search for spaces where that identity is validated. The Right stepped into that vacuum.
## **A Better Way Forward**
Recognizing this dynamic does not mean abandoning progress. Equality is not the problem. Justice is not the problem. But messaging matters.
If the goal is to build a healthier society, we need to offer young men a vision of masculinity that includes dignity and purpose. Positive masculinity does not mean returning to rigid gender hierarchies. It means redefining strength in ways that include responsibility, empathy, and respect.
Young men should be told it is okay to work hard, to be ambitious, and to take pride in providing for the people they love. But success does not diminish when others succeed alongside them. Protecting the women you love does not mean controlling them. It means defending their right to make their own choices.
The deeper message young men need to hear is surprisingly simple: it is okay to be a man. No one is trying to erase masculinity. Strength, empathy, responsibility, and respect are not contradictions. They are the foundations of a healthy society.
Because when success is no longer treated as a zero-sum game--when people believe opportunity can expand rather than simply shift--the fear that drives so much resentment begins to lose its power.
And when that fear fades, the politics built on it begin to lose their grip as well.
### **TL;DR**
Young men didn't suddenly become reactionary. They were recruited. The manosphere, conservative media, and right-wing politics built a pipeline that takes insecurity about status, identity, and success and turns it into resentment. Democrats expanded rights and opportunity--but often failed to explain how young men still fit into that future. Understanding the insecurity pipeline from the manosphere to the ballot box Mar 16 | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Everyone in politics is asking the same question right now: why are Democrats losing young men? More specifically, why are so many young men gravitating toward what people call the "manosphere"--the online ecosystem of influencers, podcasts, and personalities built around hyper-masculine identity, grievance politics, and reactionary culture. A lot of people try to explain this through economics. They say young men feel left behind financially, that wages are stagnant, that housing is unaffordable, and that stable careers are harder to find. All of that is true. But I think the deeper issue is something more psychological. It is about the perceived opportunity to be successful in this country: successful financially, successful as someone who can take care of a family, and successful in terms of status and identity--strong instead of weak, respected instead of emasculated. At its core, this whole dynamic is about belonging to the pack. The manosphere has become very good at reinforcing that pack mentality, tapping directly into one of the most primal fears young men have: the fear that if you fall behind, you will be left behind. Thrown out in the cold. Left out of the tribe. For years Democrats have talked about leveling the playing field and expanding rights. Those are good goals and necessary ones. But while we were doing that, the Right--and an entire ecosystem of influencers--were telling young men a very different story. They told them something simple: that they are losing something before they ever even had the chance to have it. When you frame the world that way, it feels deeply unfair. The story these men hear over and over again is that society is designed to make sure they never succeed, and worse, that they will be left behind. The Theology of Dominance One of the ways these insecurities get reinforced is through religion. Over the past several decades, a particular strain of Christianity has become very influential in American politics, especially through the rise of the Evangelical Right, Christian Nationalism, and the Prosperity Gospel. Figures like Jerry Falwell and Pat Robertson helped popularize a worldview where masculinity is not simply natural but divinely ordained dominance. Men are told they are supposed to lead, supposed to dominate, supposed to control. If that hierarchy is challenged, it is framed not merely as social change but as an attack on God's design. And once you frame it that way, it becomes extremely difficult to argue against. After all, how do you argue with God? This is not the same set of Christian values emphasized in many other traditions. In Catholic, Methodist, and Episcopal communities, the emphasis is often placed on service, humility, and dignity for all people. But the version amplified in political media often sounds very different: God blessed me by letting me be born in the United States, and I have the freedom to do whatever I can to make it. Success becomes proof of righteousness. Power becomes proof of virtue. Hierarchy becomes holy. The Fear of Replacement Most of these men do not hate women. Many of them want the same things previous generations of men wanted: relationships, families, stability, and the sense that hard work will lead somewhere. But they are also being told that as women gain opportunities and advance professionally, their own chances at achieving those same dreams are shrinking. They fear they will be forced to step aside. They fear they will be replaced. For decades, young men were raised with a fairly clear expectation of adulthood: work hard, earn a decent wage, support a family, and society will recognize your role as a provider. But the economic system that supported that model has been eroding for years. Wages have stagnated, housing costs have exploded, and stable careers are harder to find. The path to adulthood now feels far less certain than it did for their parents. Into that uncertainty, right-wing media offers a very convenient explanation. You are not struggling because the system changed. You are struggling because someone else took your place. Take the panic around the term DEI. Why does it scare so many men? Because they are told that DEI is not about expanding opportunity but about demoting them. The argument they hear constantly is simple: those opportunities have to come from somewhere, so they must be taken from you. In that narrative, every promotion given to a woman becomes proof that men are being pushed out, every scholarship aimed at historically excluded communities becomes evidence that the system is rigged, and every diversity initiative becomes another symbol of their supposed decline. Emotionally, that translates into something very tangible: less money, less opportunity, less respect, and less likelihood of building a stable life. Perhaps most powerful of all is the fear of looking like a failure. For generations, masculinity has been tied to the ability to provide. When that role feels threatened, the fear becomes existential. If they cannot fulfill the version of manhood they were raised to expect, then who exactly are they supposed to be? The Right does not try to resolve that anxiety. It weaponizes it. Young men are told something simple: you did not fall behind, you were pushed, and someone else took what should have been yours. The Scarcity Mindset The same psychological dynamic appears in immigration debates. If you asked most of these young men for a detailed policy solution to immigration, they probably would not have one. They are not thinking about visa systems, asylum law, or labor markets. What they are reacting to is something much older: the belief that someone unknown is coming to take what belongs to them. Whenever people believe resources are limited, the instinct to guard what you have becomes powerful. Immigration is often framed through that lens. The emotional reaction is not really about the jobs immigrants take, but about what those jobs represent. Their own families may have taken those same jobs generations ago, but history rarely feels relevant in moments of insecurity. What matters is perception. And the emotional logic becomes very simple: so what? It is mine now. If someone else gets it, that means I lost. That kind of thinking turns opportunity into a zero-sum game. If someone else rises, it must mean you are falling. The Right has spent years reinforcing that narrative. Immigration becomes not a complex policy issue but a direct threat to personal stability and identity. Masculinity and the Culture War The same insecurity helps explain the intensity of today's culture wars. Why do some men react so strongly to being called "gay" or "weak"? Why does the existence of trans people provoke such visceral reactions from people who insist it has nothing to do with them? For many of these men, the answer comes down to hierarchy. They were raised with a model of masculinity that works like a ranking system. At the top sits the ideal man: strong, successful, emotionally unshakeable, and clearly in control. Everything else sits somewhere below that standard. When cultural norms shift and those boundaries blur, it can feel like the structure itself is under attack. Being called weak is not simply an insult; it is an accusation that someone has fallen down the social ladder. Once someone believes their identity is under threat, the conversation stops being about policy or social norms and becomes about survival. The Influencer Pipeline This is where the internet becomes incredibly powerful. When young boys say something ignorant or make a bad joke--as kids often do--the reaction they receive can shape how they interpret the culture around them. Sometimes that reaction is constructive. But online, it is often immediate condemnation. For a teenager trying to figure out where he fits in the world, that can feel less like correction and more like rejection. That moment of friction is exactly where the influencer pipeline begins. Right-wing content creators are extremely good at identifying that feeling and exploiting it. They step in and say: they hate you, but we don't. Suddenly someone who felt embarrassed or rejected finds an entire online culture celebrating the exact behavior he was criticized for. What was once criticism becomes validation. What was once embarrassment becomes identity. Over time, podcasts, livestreams, and social media personalities build an ecosystem where exaggerated masculinity becomes entertainment. At first it is framed as comedy--just jokes, just guys being guys. But gradually humor turns into grievance, grievance turns into ideology, and the algorithm rewards whoever pushes the boundary further. Eventually defensiveness hardens into identity. The Political Validation Eventually those cultural frustrations move into politics. That is where someone like Donald Trump enters the picture. For many young men already immersed in this ecosystem, Trump does not just look like a political candidate. He looks like validation. He says the same things they have been hearing for years: that elites are mocking them, immigrants are taking their jobs, the system is rigged, and masculinity is under attack. The message resonates not because it is sophisticated but because it feels familiar. Trump reinforces the deeper worldview at the center of the movement: that life is a competition between winners and losers. Strength is everything. Weakness deserves ridicule. Success is not something shared; it is something conquered. Supporting him becomes less about policy and more about recognition. He speaks their language. He validates their frustration. He gives their insecurity a political home. Where We Went Wrong So where did we go wrong? The answer is complicated. Many of the social changes that expanded opportunity were necessary and long overdue. But somewhere along the line, our cultural conversation about masculinity shifted in a way that many young men interpreted as rejection rather than reform. Instead of saying masculinity should evolve, the conversation sometimes sounded like masculinity itself was the problem. The difference between toxic masculinity and masculinity itself became blurred. What many young men heard was not "be better," but "be less"--less aggressive, less competitive, less masculine. When identity feels attacked, people rarely respond by embracing criticism. They search for spaces where that identity is validated. The Right stepped into that vacuum. A Better Way Forward Recognizing this dynamic does not mean abandoning progress. Equality is not the problem. Justice is not the problem. But messaging matters. If the goal is to build a healthier society, we need to offer young men a vision of masculinity that includes dignity and purpose. Positive masculinity does not mean returning to rigid gender hierarchies. It means redefining strength in ways that include responsibility, empathy, and respect. Young men should be told it is okay to work hard, to be ambitious, and to take pride in providing for the people they love. But success does not diminish when others succeed alongside them. Protecting the women you love does not mean controlling them. It means defending their right to make their own choices. The deeper message young men need to hear is surprisingly simple: it is okay to be a man. No one is trying to erase masculinity. Strength, empathy, responsibility, and respect are not contradictions. They are the foundations of a healthy society. Because when success is no longer treated as a zero-sum game--when people believe opportunity can expand rather than simply shift--the fear that drives so much resentment begins to lose its power. And when that fear fades, the politics built on it begin to lose their grip as well. TL;DR Young men didn't suddenly become reactionary. They were recruited. The manosphere, conservative media, and right-wing politics built a pipeline that takes insecurity about status, identity, and success and turns it into resentment. Democrats expanded rights and opportunity--but often failed to explain how young men still fit into that future. Until we offer a version of masculinity that includes strength, dignity, and purpose without domination, that pipeline will keep filling. What is By the Ballot? I was on CNBC last week talking about AI and jobs. I painted a foreboding picture of corporate layoffs that have just kicked off. Indeed, Oracle and Amazon just announced that they would likely cut more than 30,000 workers between them. One of the anchors, Becky Quick, asked me,
"So what do we do?"
I [answered](https://substack.com/redirect/74c589f6-9245-4121-94a9-a8a5b3f08d6c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), "We generally tax things we want less of. In this situation, we want to preserve labor in every corner and environment. So we should stop taxing labor and instead take the advice of Dario Amodei, the CEO of Anthropic, and start taxing AI." This could be used to fund Universal Basic Income among other measures.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a0b6f9db-e670-4378-be8b-86dd238d5593?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Dario Amodei, in the past number of weeks, has been saying two things: First, his company, which produces Claude, is going to automate up to 50% of entry-level white-collar jobs in the next several years. Second, he thinks his company should be taxed on it. He suggests a 3% of revenue 'token tax,' which could raise billions very quickly.
That's right, one of the biggest AI CEOs thinks we should tax his company.
Why don't legislators take him up on this suggestion?
Right now, lawmakers lack any real vision for how to deal with AI except to cheerlead and pave the way for data centers. The AI lobby has compiled $185 million, which makes them a feared industry to get on the wrong side of.
Meanwhile, the favorability rate of AI among Americans is only 26%. This is lower than, for example, the rating for ICE.
The argument I made on CNBC is that a popular backlash is coming and some kind of sensible taxing of AI is going to be necessary. The argument that "we can't interfere with the AI industry for fear of losing the competition to China" ignores the facts that 1. This competition won't be won on the last dollar spent, but on the models' abilities to improve themselves and whether there's a real moat and 2. Chinese and American AI are already separating into two ecosystems and spheres of influence.
My comments on CNBC went viral, in part because of both the logic and the appeal. Who would be mad at taxing AI instead of people, especially when at least one of the companies is literally asking for it? It would make both workers and employers happy and put more money into people's hands. It would also help preserve millions of jobs in a time when that should be the top priority. Whether our putative leaders can understand this vision and make it happen is one of the big questions; it may be that someone has to force their hand.
Go to [noblemobile.com/yang](https://substack.com/redirect/1950db23-0568-4540-9933-035024bb4673?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for 3 months off your wireless bill, the best deal around, that will also reduce your screen time and help you save for your family. The [Hudson Valley Ideas Fest](https://substack.com/redirect/ae596c6e-1639-43aa-b656-3fb99eb5c9e5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) returns to Rosendale, NY on April 25th! Go outside and look up.
