Hey folks,
**Adam Mockler** and I jumped on for a bonus Saturday episode because there was a lot to unpack this week. We dug into the Laura Loomer story blowing up right now, but we also talked about something deeper: what happens when conspiracy theorists and bigots get real political power. I shared my own history with Loomer--it tells you everything you need to know about how the MAGA machine works.
**Here are a few moments from the conversation:**
* **00:01:07** Adam lays out the breaking news: Trump loyalist Laura Loomer gets confronted by Indian journalists over her racist and Islamophobic comments at the India Today Conclave.
* **00:03:28** I walk through my own years-long fight with Loomer--how a conspiracy theory she pushed led to congressional subpoenas, harassment of my staff, and even threats against my family.
* **00:07:03** The clip that set this off: a journalist directly challenges Loomer's Islamophobia after one of her most vile tweets about Muslim TSA agents.
* **00:12:07** We talk about the scary part: Loomer's real influence inside Trump's orbit--from pushing for intelligence officials to be fired to influencing policy decisions.
* **00:18:06** Adam shares his family's immigration story and we talk about what actually makes America strong--and why diversity and pluralism are core American values.

This episode is about more than one extremist influencer. It's about the ecosystem that empowers people like her--and the damage that happens when conspiracy theories and bigotry become political strategy. Peter,
We alone can stop the SAVE Act, or as it should be called "Jim Crow 2.0".
Not hyperbole. Not fundraising rhetoric. Cold, hard truth.
The SAVE Act - Trump's Jim Crow 2.0 voter suppression scheme - is barreling through Congress right now with full MAGA support. Lauren Boebert is championing it. Colorado Republicans are lining up behind it. And if it passes, millions of Americans will be stripped of their right to vote.
Elderly citizens without birth certificates. Low-income voters who can't afford to track down documents. Native Americans with incomplete records. Naturalized citizens who've misplaced paperwork over decades.
All disenfranchised. All silenced. All part of the plan.

## **THANK YOU, SENATOR BENSON!**
As Senator Joanne C. Benson announces that she will not seek re-election to the Maryland General Assembly, our community pauses to recognize and thank her for decades of dedicated public service to the people of District 24 and Prince George’s County.For many years, Senator Benson has answered the call to serve, advocating for our community and representing our district in Annapolis with commitment and determination. Public service requires perseverance, sacrifice, and a deep belief in the people you represent. Through her long career, Senator Benson has demonstrated those values and helped shape the course of our community.Throughout her time in office, Senator Benson has been a voice for the residents of District 24 and a steady presence in our public life. Her leadership reflects a lifetime commitment to service, and her work has contributed to the strength, stability, and progress of Prince George’s County. Generations of residents have benefited from leaders who were willing to step forward and dedicate themselves to the public good, and Senator Benson’s career stands as part of that proud tradition.District 24 is stronger because of the foundation that has been built through years of leadership and service. As our community reflects on this moment of transition, we are reminded that public service is a continuing responsibility—one generation building upon the work of those who came before. The progress of our community depends on honoring that legacy while continuing to move forward with purpose.On behalf of my family, and the many residents who care deeply about the future of our community, we extend our sincere gratitude to Senator Benson for her years of service. We thank her for the example she has set and for the dedication she has shown to the people of our district.We wish Senator Benson continued success and fulfillment in the next chapter of her journey, and I remain committed to continuing the work of strengthening our families, uplifting our neighborhoods, and ensuring that District 24 remains a strong and vibrant community for generations to come.**AGAIN, THANK YOU!** – [Kevin Ford Jr](https://z6h1.engage.squarespace-mail.com/r?m=69b830adc502166d43b01e6b&u=https%3A%2F%2Fvotekevinford.com%2Fmeetkevin%3Fss_source%3Dsscampaigns%26ss_campaign_id%3D69b108067a19e35a75a20a01%26ss_email_id%3D69b830adc502166d43b01e6b%26ss_campaign_name%3DTHANK%2BYOU%252C%2BSEN.%2BBENSON%2521%2521%26ss_campaign_sent_date%3D2026-03-16T16%253A35%253A12Z&w=67e59626f08d7b1924bf5048&c=b_69b108067a19e35a75a20a01&l=en-US&s=1ddjQ59-yGyYBKenblEvw1kNxF0%3D)

Peter,
Families across this country are still living with fear and instability, and the climate crisis is getting worse. Masked ICE agents are being sent into our neighborhoods, ripping families apart and terrorizing communities. The cost of living keeps rising, and people can't afford basic needs like healthcare, housing, or groceries, while communities are facing intensifying wildfires, floods, and heat waves.
Instead of confronting the climate crisis and helping communities prepare and recover, this administration continues to hand out giveaways to billionaires and immunity to big oil companies – letting the corporations responsible for climate pollution avoid accountability. Everyday people are left to bear the costs of climate disasters, rising energy bills, and polluted air and water.
This is not the America we were promised. Will you join us on Saturday, March 28th for No Kings National Day of Nonviolent Action? Check here to find an event near you. [https://www.nokings.org/]
Find your event [https://www.nokings.org/]
Across the country, people are coming together in morally grounded, nonviolent direct action to demand a different path forward: one where our leaders stand with communities, not corporate polluters.
We’re showing this president and the world that our country does not belong to greedy billionaires or the fossil fuel companies fueling the climate crisis. It belongs to the people, and to the generations who will inherit the planet we leave behind.
No Thrones. No Crowns. No Kings!
In solidarity,

clean_body: [] Peter, Families across this country are still living with fear and instability, and the climate crisis is getting worse. Masked ICE agents are being sent into our neighborhoods, ripping families apart and terrorizing communities. The cost of living keeps rising, and people can't afford basic needs like healthcare, housing, or groceries, while communities are facing intensifying wildfires, floods, and heat waves. Instead of confronting the climate crisis and helping communities prepare and recover, this administration continues to hand out giveaways to billionaires and immunity to big oil companies – letting the corporations responsible for climate pollution avoid accountability. Everyday people are left to bear the costs of climate disasters, rising energy bills, and polluted air and water. This is not the America we were promised. Will you join us on Saturday, March 28th for No Kings National Day of Nonviolent Action? Check here to find an event near you. [] Find your event [] Across the country, people are coming together in morally grounded, nonviolent direct action to demand a different path forward: one where our leaders stand with communities, not corporate polluters. We’re showing this president and the world that our country does not belong to greedy billionaires or the fossil fuel companies fueling the climate crisis. It belongs to the people, and to the generations who will inherit the planet we leave behind. No Thrones. No Crowns. No Kings! That debate took place on January 21 at the [North Oakland Republican Club](https://jrhsf9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001Yl6yZvRl5B08vQMZBUQt5Mdxd1rvTh3RG0KIbBLCfBmdGHRxVfZOcWnOJz7-a4pBAVAkS7JMCCKfWBrBcW-ZtDzvhKiNYtqueGrlT_cyFDObGgglqYpInQPMSf5u2wnq8m9zRhvvoKbN-fbxcP0bbljV0h61PWiESlZe52gLt4KbHrJhlcufAouJD3IQ2Yu_&c=HlbUt8Ir6PuONVVlTYQ5992tnZAY5JHPg2OJisGf7unru3EoDp5zGQ==&ch=LCGjTyZD3w-aXZEZFvwxG_uFizLvd1M5Rna1z_SeTKyVQtJ6wO3DBw==), in my opponent's own backyard. It was the first real opportunity for delegates to hear the candidates side-by-side, answer questions in real time, and test the strength of our ideas.
Since that debate, my opponent has refused to participate in additional scheduled debates and joint forums before the nominating convention.
My opponent has said that delegates have already had "ample opportunities" to hear from the candidates. (MIRS.new - February 18)
Delegates decide when they've heard enough. Not the candidates.
That is why I have continued to attend forums, accept debate invitations, and make myself available to answer questions directly.
Forums introduce candidates. Debates test them.
Anyone can deliver prepared remarks in a forum or solo appearance. A debate allows delegates to see how a candidate performs under pressure, answers difficult questions, and responds when challenged. A debate also gives candidates the opportunity to challenge misleading statements or misinformation and set the record straight.
That matters in a race for Attorney General.
In the courtroom, lawyers present evidence, argue the law, and defend the merits of their case. When the facts are misstated or the law is misrepresented, someone objects.
Debates are the closest thing to that process in a campaign.
Throughout this race, I have honored my commitments to attend events, meet delegates, and answer questions directly. I often arrive early, stay late, and make myself available for calls because delegates deserve the opportunity to look "under the hood" before casting their vote.
Unfortunately, my opponent has chosen a different approach. If a candidate is unwilling to debate a fellow Republican exercising professional courtesy and restraint, it raises a serious question: how will that candidate perform against the Democratic nominee in November?
Michigan Republicans need a nominee who is prepared for that fight.
A recent [Ballenger Report](https://jrhsf9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001Yl6yZvRl5B08vQMZBUQt5Mdxd1rvTh3RG0KIbBLCfBmdGHRxVfZOcWnOJz7-a4pB84H5W9Dnh9jRgMYYQKiZUNpcLwvjPR107N2gPfH2cEQIoW_n6wn1AV3nCZ2Lyfd1GnRluW4cvRxKC0M4J3NK69W4pEh2zm2RKQJ_Iao07jSyUFO4uZPQAYIXMClBkCi6x5uPlDV-Cy1tbLdTqgm87CWwIOL0eiSX&c=HlbUt8Ir6PuONVVlTYQ5992tnZAY5JHPg2OJisGf7unru3EoDp5zGQ==&ch=LCGjTyZD3w-aXZEZFvwxG_uFizLvd1M5Rna1z_SeTKyVQtJ6wO3DBw==) noted that I am the only Republican candidate for Attorney General with a viable path to winning the general election.
With your support, we will win this race.
Doug Lloyd Eaton County Prosecuting Attorney Candidate for Michigan Attorney General

name: Redistricting Action HQ
subject: How 2020 election deniers are working to take over the midterms
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY THE NATIONAL REDISTRICTING ACTION FUND
body:
Help us put an end to the extreme, unrelenting attacks on our democracy.
|
---

Peter,
Chances are, you've never heard of Cleta Mitchell or her organization, the Election Integrity Network. But we've all heard a lot about what they’re up to.
Cleta Mitchell — Trump’s close advisor and former attorney — and her organization have been urging the White House to declare a national emergency and take over the midterm elections. She’s also been lobbying senators every day to pass the extreme, anti-voter Save America Act.

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. A few short years ago, just months before the good people of Pennsylvania elected me as their Governor in 2022, we were running a campaign that looked a little bit different from our opponent’s.
We showed up everywhere. We treated everyone with respect. We brought more people into the fold of this movement than ever before. And Derek, on Election Day, we didn’t just win. We won in places that hadn’t voted for a Democrat in a long, long time.

# Private credit exec admits valuations are wrong
A senior executive at Apollo Global Management has bluntly admitted that[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/7bcc314e-6870-4d26-868e-18a333ea02ba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[valuations across much of the private credit and private equity industry](https://substack.com/redirect/7bcc314e-6870-4d26-868e-18a333ea02ba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** are wrong, warning that many assets are significantly overstated as defaults begin to appear.

---|---|---
* **Marks are wrong:** John Zito, co-president of Apollo's asset management arm, stated he thinks all the marks are wrong and that private equity marks in particular are inaccurate.
* **Overstated valuations:** Many software companies bought by private equity between 2018 and 2022 were acquired at much higher valuations than comparable public firms despite being lower quality.
* **Recovery warning:** Loans to a typical leveraged mid-size software company could recover only 20 to 40 cents on the dollar if the economy slows and defaults rise.
* **Trust at risk:** Zito warned that failing to properly mark down assets could cause investors to lose trust, saying Apollo intends to be a market leader in accurate marking.

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127444462/608082996/-153530995?refcode=EM_C_2603126fellow_N_SB_90DO_5_NG_N_LOGO&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84Nzg0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiOTNlODdmNy02MTIxLWYxMTEtOWE0OC0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=vQNsiFdpM-ebyNggNpJBcr6N3wylrM-plWwVNOCUafw=) Hi Peter,

I am proud to announce that my campaign will be participating as a partner in the 2026 National Democracy Summer School! This one-of-a-kind Democratic Fellowship—founded by Congressman Jamie Raskin and expanded across the country in an historic partnership with the DCCC—is dedicated to recruiting thousands of high school and college-age students and training them as the next generation of Democratic political activists and leaders.

[**As part of this educational and political initiative, I am looking for dedicated high school and college students to join me here in Ohio as Democracy Summer Fellows!**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127444464/608082999/-1821365250?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84Nzg0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiOTNlODdmNy02MTIxLWYxMTEtOWE0OC0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=vQNsiFdpM-ebyNggNpJBcr6N3wylrM-plWwVNOCUafw=&emci=84097e6f-421e-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&emdi=b93e87f7-6121-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&ceid=23746811) [APPLY HERE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127444468/608083001/-1821365250?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84Nzg0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiOTNlODdmNy02MTIxLWYxMTEtOWE0OC0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=vQNsiFdpM-ebyNggNpJBcr6N3wylrM-plWwVNOCUafw=&emci=84097e6f-421e-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&emdi=b93e87f7-6121-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&ceid=23746811) This six-week program will take place from Monday, June 22nd to Friday, August 7th and requires a commitment of 10-15 hours per week. Fellows will participate in exciting online seminars and a powerful curriculum designed by Congressman Raskin, while also organizing on-the-ground with my campaign here in Ohio.

Throughout the academic portion, Fellows will learn from academic luminaries, inspiring political leaders, policy experts, issue advocates and top community organizers from all across the country. Past Democracy Summer speakers have included House Speaker Nancy Pelosi, Professor Laurence Tribe, Senator Elizabeth Warren, Rep. Bennie Thompson, Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, and the late Rep. I launched United for Virginia’s Future PAC to support leaders who are focused on affordability, accountability, and steady leadership in Virginia and across the country. 150 poop trucks a day.
That's just some of the bad news we discussed at a local town hall in Tremont, Pennsylvania this weekend, where the community gathered to discuss the mega detention facility ICE and Dan Meuser are planning for the west end of Schuylkill County.
If there was any doubt before that this was a terrible idea - it's gone.
Tremont already feels like a dumping ground, whether it's the landfills or the sludge company that has brought nothing but a strong stench. People can't leave their windows open or sit on their porch.
And now Dan Meuser wants to help the federal government bring in a 7,500-person mega facility.
Even though the local roads (not to mention the local people) can't handle the 150 trucks a day that would be required to remove sewage from the complex.
Even though there already isn't enough water in the ground for the people who live in Tremont, let alone the 900,000 gallons a day needed for a facility this size.
Even though there's no local police force and just one ambulance service, which would have to take on an estimated 16 to 32 EMS calls for the 7,500 people who, ICE says, will spend more than a month at a time in the former Big Lots warehouse distribution center.
Even though the local child care center - the only one in the community - would likely close.
I talked with Joyce, the owner of Kids-R-Kids Child Care Center, at the town hall on Friday. She told me the ICE facility will be the end of her business - parents are already saying they'll pull their kids out if this facility goes forward.
She reached out to Meuser for help. He never got back to her.

| | SNAP and food assistance programs are under assault from every angle. Last year, Trump, with the help of Republicans in Congress, defunded SNAP and forced millions of Americans to go without the food assistance they rely on. Thankfully, that funding has been restored, for now. But there's another threat looming over SNAP that too often gets ignored. It's a little-known practice called "SNAP skimming," in which hackers and thieves target electronic SNAP cards to steal benefits. For years, I've been pressing the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) to implement bare minimum cybersecurity standards for SNAP cards, just like credit cards have. And earlier this month, I introduced a bipartisan bill to do just that. This is a no-brainer solution to protect this critical lifeline. **Families relying on food assistance are already walking an economic tightrope.** The last thing they should have to worry about is having their food assistance stolen. Republicans talk a big game about rooting out waste and fraud, and this is a perfect example of an issue that should be bipartisan. A recent report issued by the USDA itself estimates that over $555 million in SNAP benefits could be stolen in the coming years if more isn't done to enhance their cybersecurity. My legislation would put a stop to hackers and thieves ripping off the most vulnerable and American taxpayers. So I'm doing all I can to protect SNAP and those on it from further damage. That's one of the reasons I'm introducing legislation to crack down on SNAP card skimming. **Cybersecurity shouldn't depend on income or zip code.** It's time to overhaul this two-tier system that leaves families in need even more vulnerable with outdated technology. _Not when the other side is throwing everything they’ve got at you._
_Not when President Trump makes you a personal target._
**That’s where things stand here in North Carolina ahead of the midterm elections.**
Our election is the most competitive U.S. Senate race anywhere in the country — it’s the one that will determine whether or not we can take back the Senate for the people and break the GOP’s one-party hold on Washington.
President Trump and his political allies are targeting me. Far-right PACs and mega donors are lined up to pour hundreds of millions into defeating me. _But I know that we can win._
You see, I’ve won some of the most competitive statewide races here in battleground NC. In fact, _I have never lost a race._ Over and over, we’ve won _together_ — and that’s how we’ll win again.

name: Amy Klobuchar
subject: I need to know if you’re with me
disclaimer_text: paid for by Minnesotans for Klobuchar committee
body:
My work has always been powered by our grassroots team, so I’m counting on you.
#
[](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22437?source=em20260316-1526&t=1&akid=1526%2E2118727%2EMBj29G)
I’m running for governor of the state of Minnesota.
**My work has always been powered by our grassroots team, so I need to know:[Can I count on your support?](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22437?source=em20260316-1526&t=2&akid=1526%2E2118727%2EMBj29G)**
**[ADD YOUR NAME ››](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22437?source=em20260316-1526&t=3&akid=1526%2E2118727%2EMBj29G)**
I believe we must stand up for what’s right and fix what’s wrong. That’s why I’m running for governor.
I am running for every Minnesotan who wants to buy their first home, for every parent who wants a better world for their kids, for everyone who wants more affordable healthcare and for every student, farmer, dreamer and builder.
**But to accomplish everything we’re setting out to do, I need your support.**
[**This is a home-grown campaign, born in a moment like no other. It is for people who believe in something bigger than ourselves. So please: If you’re with me, add your name today.**](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22437?source=em20260316-1526&t=4&akid=1526%2E2118727%2EMBj29G)
Minnesota, I want to be a transformative governor. Now is our moment to renew our commitment to the common good. I’m asking you to look up to the North Star and to see that there is a better future before us.
To pursue good, we must believe that good will prevail. I know I do -- and that’s why I’m asking you to join us.
Thank you.
Amy

_**by Ellie Leonard, BAM Contributing Editor**_
_**Trigger warning: this article contains limited descriptions of abuse**_
When the DOJ handed us three of four missing 302s--code for "FBI interviews"--from a young teen out of the Southeast, it didn't really feel like a lot to go on. We knew they'd been hidden for a reason. After all, this was the second major case implicating Donald Trump and Jeffrey Epstein together for sexual abuse of a child. But we didn't have much to work with, and what we did have all occurred in the early 1980s, pre-internet, and with a number of details that felt out of place for who we'd come to know as the early 2000s middle-aged millionaire sex predator.
But even with very little information, the FBI had taken "Jane Doe 4" seriously, interviewing her at least four times. It was only recently that NPR reporters discovered the missing 53 pages of Doe's 302s, leading to an uproar, and eventually the DOJ handing us 16 more pages, the remaining 37 still nowhere to be found. But not only did the FBI take this woman seriously, but she was now represented by Lisa Bloom, daughter of Gloria Allred, and lawyer for one of the most significant cases in this entire investigation: Katie Johnson.
So with my laptop in hand, some late nights, and a whole lot of coffee, I dug in. I wanted to see if this case was provable, disprovable, or simply a question mark swallowed up by time.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d1467979-ed30-4df0-8354-50a9d14d9c28?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
FBI Interview 1 - July 24, 2019
To summarize, Jane Doe 4 arrived at an unknown island in 1981, where her mother was hired as a broker for a real estate firm managing vacation homes in the Sea Pines Plantation. This clarified that we were talking about Hilton Head Island, South Carolina. At 13, the girl attended school with her siblings, and was encouraged by her mother to make babysitting fliers to hand out to visitors and long-term renters for a little extra cash. She did, and quickly got her first call, a man she remembered only as "Jeff." When she arrived, there were no children, and "Jeff" offered her alcohol, marijuana, and cocaine. After that, things got hazy, but she knew he sexually abused her, and could only think how pleased her friends would be that she'd found someone to give them drugs.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6ba0df9a-cc08-4f06-839f-075864928660?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Hilton Head High School's yearbook, 1985
This continued over the course of two or three years, and often included other men, old and overweight, wealthy, and often physically abusive. The only one she ever named was "Jim Atkins," but often shut down the interviews, too upset to say any more. Epstein had a woman with him at times, though not likely a partner in the traditional sense. She "wasn't black or Caucasian," Doe remembered, but came off as very "cold."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/72861aee-a536-4825-843f-59b540a652af?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Ghislaine Maxwell in the 1980s
At some point, Doe found pictures of herself in one of "Jeff's" drawers, Polaroids that he'd taken on a tripod when the young girl was naked. It was this moment that set off a chain of events, leading to her mother's criminal conviction on the island. But we'll come back to that.
I started piecing apart this investigation with tiny details, unique but simple things Doe included in her statements that might otherwise appear like they don't matter. She mentioned a crinkly "cardboard shirt" he made her wear during one of their "between 6 and 20" interactions. She said her mother had a house somewhere nearby, one she'd bought for $55,000 in 1981. One of the abusive men had stomped her toe. She'd gone to a Rick James concert in Savannah and bumped into "Jeff," who offered to drive her home, but dropped her off miles away. When the police picked her up, they'd fed her fried chicken. She couldn't remember if he was called "Jeff Epstein" or not, but remembered he looked like Lurch from the Addams Family, very long in the face. And when he got angry, he lisped and she could see he had a snaggle tooth in the back of his mouth.
* * *
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=190997935&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTkwOTk3OTM1LCJpYXQiOjE3NzM2ODc4MDAsImV4cCI6MTc3NjI3OTgwMCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.hjFC8mD38fpG6OCgP0euG4ocg5evkAX-9c0s7C4fmxw)
* * *
Doe's mother passed away a long time ago, and she never told anyone else except a close friend what had happened to her when she was 13, maybe 14 years old, and in the years after. And when Jeffrey Epstein was arrested in July, 2019, her friend gave her a call, reminding Doe what she'd said all those years ago. At some point she agreed to come forward, but she still wouldn't mention anything about Donald Trump. And when the only picture she had to show agents the man named "Jeff" included Trump, she requested that the agents crop the President out.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c0ac5306-3ff7-4bca-bef4-e32b9de308a6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
But the friend remembered what Doe said, that at some point "Jeff" had taken her to New York, into office buildings, big homes, and she was chided and abused by Donald Trump. He made fun of her for being a tomboy, just as Epstein had made fun of her overly large breasts, making the girl extremely self-conscious. And without going into detail, Doe's experience with Donald Trump deeply reflected the same experience had by Katie Johnson, that not only included sexual abuse but physical as well.
And now we had a case that was, again, seemingly credible according to FBI records, and also credible enough to be represented by a major law firm representing other Epstein and Trump survivors.
So I started at the very beginning. They'd moved to the island in 1981, when her mother purchased a house for $55,000. I didn't have her mother's name, so I'd have to go in another direction before I could dig for a deed.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4364b2ec-977c-43a8-a62c-3eb7600a9ebe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
According to Doe, her mother had been charged with embezzling money. She was very up front about both her and her mother's criminal histories, issues with sobriety, and frequent moves, marriages, and divorces. Doe wanted to be credible, but knew a woman in her position would have to fight. So I looked for the case, using archived copies of the Island Packet Newspaper, and I found it. Her mother had embezzled $22,000. But according to Doe it wasn't a simple case of stealing. She'd eventually told her mother about the abuse and the pictures in "Jeff's" drawer. And Doe's mother tried to get everything back, anything she could do to protect her daughter, stealing money to give to the young, wealthy New Yorker who vacationed on the island.
This takes us back to Jim Atkins.
Jim Atkins, as described in Doe's interviews, was Jeff's wealthy friend from Ohio. He was the "money guy" or something involved in education, maybe a dean, someone on the board, but connected with a "for-profit" college out of Cincinnati. I dug for schools, bypassing the major universities and checking every board of regents, board of trustees, administrations, faculty, donors, you name it. And then we found him--yes, we; it's a team effort--Jimmy L. Atkins of Fort Mitchell, Kentucky. He was director of the now defunct Betz College Inc. and Betz Business School. He also owned Harbour Homes Realty, which managed most of Sea Pines Plantation, and was Doe's mother's boss. They'd also dated, she claimed, likely an affair hidden from his wife back in Ohio.
* * *

* * *
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e8440be2-a32a-47ad-b07d-8aafdbc968b8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I found the school records, the ownership records, and the records of Doe's mother's embezzlement case. And something definitely felt off, as indicated by her lawyer in the newspaper.
> #### "[I am] dismayed by the fact that the commission has acted in such an arbitrary and capricious manner by revoking [REDACTED]'s license, without any opportunity for her to be heard relative to the accusations. It certainly appears to me that the actions of the commission, at least at this point in time, are premature and grossly violate the basic rudiments of due process." \- Jane Doe's mother's attorney
> | [](https://substack.com/redirect/7ef17231-fa72-40ba-b909-83136d3a5653?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
> ---|---|---
In short, Jimmy Atkins had bypassed all due process when it came to a full audit and chance for Doe's mother to state her case, pulling the plug on everything immediately. This resulted in Doe's mother losing her job, and having to pay Atkins back $150/month, equivalent to $448 by today's rates. She couldn't afford it, and when threatened with jailtime, her daughter went to Atkins to beg for leniency. He told her he hoped they'd "end up in the gutter"--the man who sexually and physically abused Doe.
Eventually, Doe and her mother and siblings all moved away from Hilton Head, her mother remarried, and ended up on the West Coast. Their marriages were what you might expect, following trauma and a criminal history that would never disappear.
* * *
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.Zn6A7M6Zp6npisCS8lPqvWRdcEEK4wVP3QUzxwgJH-4?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=190997935)
* * *
At some point Doe met up with a man, maybe a roommate, maybe just a friend, and smelled cologne on him that repulsed her, triggering a memory that caused her to panic. Years later, the pair remembered the day and the cologne, "Grey Flannel," that the man had worn. History shows us that Grey Flannel peaked in popularity sometime in the 1980s, leading one to believe she would have smelled it during a moment of trauma around the same time.
And that "cardboard shirt," a weird, crinkly material called "Tyvek" that was quite popular in the '80s, and might have been worn with penny loafers, which Doe said "Jeff" wore, and would trade out often for a newer, shinier pair.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/79a6815f-d9a9-4a21-90b5-4b7104174d7f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
She remembered shelves filled with books, and classical music, but also Neil Diamond. We know now that Epstein always kept massive bookshelves, a busy reader in order to keep up his façade of knowledge in every subject, but also was an accomplished classical pianist. And Neil Diamond? His name shows up the files, innocently enough, but Epstein seemed to care about his music.
But what about the drugs? What about the gin and tonic she said he occasionally drank? That didn't seem like Epstein. Or at least not the Epstein we know in 2000, 2004, 2010, 2019. But this might have been Jeff Epstein, the young financier, the rich-but-not-so-rich guy getting his feet wet in things like overseas intelligence and billionaire tax management. He was still sociopathic and a sexual deviant, but he might've been a little less careful--maybe not the teetotaler we knew him to be in later years. She never said he took drugs, only handed them out as a kind of payment, something he replaced later with real cash. And if you look at the history of the Southeast, just as Doe said, drugs like LSD and cocaine spiked just after the early 1980s. It made her suspicious, but she didn't push.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6dfccf1b-dcb2-4ea8-b6dc-e02ee8b9bd27?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Then there was that Rick James concert, the one in Savannah when she was 15. Trickier to pin down, if I'm honest. Rick James _did_ play quite a bit in Georgia and the Southeast, but not necessarily the exact dates Doe said. He was in Savannah in 1982, when she was 12, in Atlanta in 1983, and then took a break until 1985, when the tour started back up along the East Coast. It's not a huge discrepancy, considering she's trying to remember one night 40 years ago (could you give details about that Green Day concert in the '90s?), but she wasn't far off. Maybe there are more details in the other 37 pages we still don't have.
But there was one other thing that stood out to me, and I will include a trigger warning here just for clarification. Doe mentioned that one way Epstein abused her was by tugging at her nipples, something described in multiple other survivors' interviews. A small detail, though just as damaging, but curious to hear the same form of abuse across the gamut of women's stories.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ad520fb0-72e8-4098-9e6e-93ec6566dae4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
FBI Interview 2 - August 7, 2019
When Doe finally talked about Donald Trump, a couple interviews in and encouraged by the FBI, she mentioned unique and interesting details outside of the actual abuse. She knew he had illegal building permits. And she'd heard him talking about "washing money" through his casinos. His favorite number was six. What did it mean? She didn't know.
* * *
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=190997935&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTkwOTk3OTM1LCJpYXQiOjE3NzM2ODc4MDAsImV4cCI6MTc3NjI3OTgwMCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.hjFC8mD38fpG6OCgP0euG4ocg5evkAX-9c0s7C4fmxw)
* * *
Jane Doe did her best to run from Hilton Head and the abuse that she endured there. But like most kids who never resolve their trauma, she struggled with relationships and crime. In 2023 she was arrested for taking money from a dying man saving for his funeral. She admitted it, talked to the agents up front, and the story is pretty devasting. Doe's picture shows the years, the trauma, the substance abuse, and the damage a man like "Jeff" inflicted on all those little girls. But it was also another detail Doe provided that linked to real information that I could track down.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fa277fb6-cfea-4359-95bc-cb24ceeb2ad3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Obviously we're not at the end of this story, not even close. I've reached out to the brokers and agents who worked with Doe's mother, trying to find any kind of a record that showed Jeffrey Epstein rented a vacation home or homes on Hilton Head Island in the 1980s. There are flight logs from several years later that showed he traveled to the island quite a bit, a hotspot for wealthy investors and yachting types. But nothing was digitized, and I'm sure no one thought anything of destroying a box of rental records that was four decades old.
But maybe not. Maybe there's something still there that they could find, like a little girl's babysitting flier, or a man giving piano lessons, or a wealthy young New Yorker with a long face, a snaggle tooth, and a lisp that showed up when he got upset.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/89f244fa-eabb-4265-a3d4-07d4ba14b20a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Cosmopolitan Magazine's "Bachelor of the Month" \- July, 1980
For now, we know who Jane's mother is, and when she passed, and the name of her nursing home. We know Jane and her siblings, when she was born, where, who she married, her criminal history, and the fact that she desperately wants to remain anonymous, which I will respect. But the FBI believed her enough to call her back three more times. The Bloom Firm believed her enough to represent her case.
And the DOJ believed her enough to hide 37 pages, detailing her abuse at the hands of the President of the United States.
_Jane Doe 4 sued the Epstein Estate in 2019, and later received a settlement._
#### This is an ongoing story...
* * *
_**This is why Blue Amp Media exists.**_
_Ellie spent weeks on this. Late nights, archived newspapers, property records, court filings, FBI interview transcripts -- cross-referencing details that a 13-year-old girl remembered 40 years ago against documents that the DOJ tried to keep hidden. And she found things. Verifiable, documented things. That is not nothing. That is exactly what independent journalism is supposed to do, and almost never does anymore._

And when he got angry, he lisped and she could see he had a snaggle tooth in the back of his mouth. Doe's mother passed away a long time ago, and she never told anyone else except a close friend what had happened to her when she was 13, maybe 14 years old, and in the years after. And when Jeffrey Epstein was arrested in July, 2019, her friend gave her a call, reminding Doe what she'd said all those years ago. At some point she agreed to come forward, but she still wouldn't mention anything about Donald Trump. And when the only picture she had to show agents the man named "Jeff" included Trump, she requested that the agents crop the President out. | | ---|---|--- But the friend remembered what Doe said, that at some point "Jeff" had taken her to New York, into office buildings, big homes, and she was chided and abused by Donald Trump. He made fun of her for being a tomboy, just as Epstein had made fun of her overly large breasts, making the girl extremely self-conscious. And without going into detail, Doe's experience with Donald Trump deeply reflected the same experience had by Katie Johnson, that not only included sexual abuse but physical as well. And now we had a case that was, again, seemingly credible according to FBI records, and also credible enough to be represented by a major law firm representing other Epstein and Trump survivors. So I started at the very beginning. They'd moved to the island in 1981, when her mother purchased a house for $55,000. I didn't have her mother's name, so I'd have to go in another direction before I could dig for a deed. | | ---|---|--- According to Doe, her mother had been charged with embezzling money. She was very up front about both her and her mother's criminal histories, issues with sobriety, and frequent moves, marriages, and divorces. Doe wanted to be credible, but knew a woman in her position would have to fight. So I looked for the case, using archived copies of the Island Packet Newspaper, and I found it. Her mother had embezzled $22,000. But according to Doe it wasn't a simple case of stealing. She'd eventually told her mother about the abuse and the pictures in "Jeff's" drawer. And Doe's mother tried to get everything back, anything she could do to protect her daughter, stealing money to give to the young, wealthy New Yorker who vacationed on the island. This takes us back to Jim Atkins. Jim Atkins, as described in Doe's interviews, was Jeff's wealthy friend from Ohio. He was the "money guy" or something involved in education, maybe a dean, someone on the board, but connected with a "for-profit" college out of Cincinnati. I dug for schools, bypassing the major universities and checking every board of regents, board of trustees, administrations, faculty, donors, you name it. And then we found him--yes, we; it's a team effort--Jimmy L. Atkins of Fort Mitchell, Kentucky. He was director of the now defunct Betz College Inc. and Betz Business School. He also owned Harbour Homes Realty, which managed most of Sea Pines Plantation, and was Doe's mother's boss. They'd also dated, she claimed, likely an affair hidden from his wife back in Ohio. | | ---|---|--- I found the school records, the ownership records, and the records of Doe's mother's embezzlement case. And something definitely felt off, as indicated by her lawyer in the newspaper. #### "[I am] dismayed by the fact that the commission has acted in such an arbitrary and capricious manner by revoking [REDACTED]'s license, without any opportunity for her to be heard relative to the accusations. It certainly appears to me that the actions of the commission, at least at this point in time, are premature and grossly violate the basic rudiments of due process." \- Jane Doe's mother's attorney | | ---|---|--- In short, Jimmy Atkins had bypassed all due process when it came to a full audit and chance for Doe's mother to state her case, pulling the plug on everything immediately. This resulted in Doe's mother losing her job, and having to pay Atkins back $150/month, equivalent to $448 by today's rates. She couldn't afford it, and when threatened with jailtime, her daughter went to Atkins to beg for leniency. He told her he hoped they'd "end up in the gutter"--the man who sexually and physically abused Doe. Eventually, Doe and her mother and siblings all moved away from Hilton Head, her mother remarried, and ended up on the West Coast. Their marriages were what you might expect, following trauma and a criminal history that would never disappear. At some point Doe met up with a man, maybe a roommate, maybe just a friend, and smelled cologne on him that repulsed her, triggering a memory that caused her to panic. Years later, the pair remembered the day and the cologne, "Grey Flannel," that the man had worn. History shows us that Grey Flannel peaked in popularity sometime in the 1980s, leading one to believe she would have smelled it during a moment of trauma around the same time. And that "cardboard shirt," a weird, crinkly material called "Tyvek" that was quite popular in the '80s, and might have been worn with penny loafers, which Doe said "Jeff" wore, and would trade out often for a newer, shinier pair. | | ---|---|--- She remembered shelves filled with books, and classical music, but also Neil Diamond. We know now that Epstein always kept massive bookshelves, a busy reader in order to keep up his façade of knowledge in every subject, but also was an accomplished classical pianist. And Neil Diamond? His name shows up the files, innocently enough, but Epstein seemed to care about his music. But what about the drugs? What about the gin and tonic she said he occasionally drank? That didn't seem like Epstein. Or at least not the Epstein we know in 2000, 2004, 2010, 2019. But this might have been Jeff Epstein, the young financier, the rich-but-not-so-rich guy getting his feet wet in things like overseas intelligence and billionaire tax management. He was still sociopathic and a sexual deviant, but he might've been a little less careful--maybe not the teetotaler we knew him to be in later years. She never said he took drugs, only handed them out as a kind of payment, something he replaced later with real cash. And if you look at the history of the Southeast, just as Doe said, drugs like LSD and cocaine spiked just after the early 1980s. It made her suspicious, but she didn't push. | | ---|---|--- Then there was that Rick James concert, the one in Savannah when she was 15. Trickier to pin down, if I'm honest. Rick James did play quite a bit in Georgia and the Southeast, but not necessarily the exact dates Doe said. He was in Savannah in 1982, when she was 12, in Atlanta in 1983, and then took a break until 1985, when the tour started back up along the East Coast. It's not a huge discrepancy, considering she's trying to remember one night 40 years ago (could you give details about that Green Day concert in the '90s?), but she wasn't far off. Maybe there are more details in the other 37 pages we still don't have. But there was one other thing that stood out to me, and I will include a trigger warning here just for clarification. Doe mentioned that one way Epstein abused her was by tugging at her nipples, something described in multiple other survivors' interviews. A small detail, though just as damaging, but curious to hear the same form of abuse across the gamut of women's stories. | | ---|---|--- FBI Interview 2 - August 7, 2019 When Doe finally talked about Donald Trump, a couple interviews in and encouraged by the FBI, she mentioned unique and interesting details outside of the actual abuse. She knew he had illegal building permits. And she'd heard him talking about "washing money" through his casinos. His favorite number was six. What did it mean? She didn't know. Jane Doe did her best to run from Hilton Head and the abuse that she endured there. But like most kids who never resolve their trauma, she struggled with relationships and crime. In 2023 she was arrested for taking money from a dying man saving for his funeral. She admitted it, talked to the agents up front, and the story is pretty devasting. Doe's picture shows the years, the trauma, the substance abuse, and the damage a man like "Jeff" inflicted on all those little girls. But it was also another detail Doe provided that linked to real information that I could track down. | | ---|---|--- Obviously we're not at the end of this story, not even close. I've reached out to the brokers and agents who worked with Doe's mother, trying to find any kind of a record that showed Jeffrey Epstein rented a vacation home or homes on Hilton Head Island in the 1980s. There are flight logs from several years later that showed he traveled to the island quite a bit, a hotspot for wealthy investors and yachting types. But nothing was digitized, and I'm sure no one thought anything of destroying a box of rental records that was four decades old. But maybe not. Maybe there's something still there that they could find, like a little girl's babysitting flier, or a man giving piano lessons, or a wealthy young New Yorker with a long face, a snaggle tooth, and a lisp that showed up when he got upset. | | ---|---|--- Cosmopolitan Magazine's "Bachelor of the Month" \- July, 1980 For now, we know who Jane's mother is, and when she passed, and the name of her nursing home. We know Jane and her siblings, when she was born, where, who she married, her criminal history, and the fact that she desperately wants to remain anonymous, which I will respect. But the FBI believed her enough to call her back three more times. The Bloom Firm believed her enough to represent her case. And the DOJ believed her enough to hide 37 pages, detailing her abuse at the hands of the President of the United States. Jane Doe 4 sued the Epstein Estate in 2019, and later received a settlement. This is an ongoing story... This is why Blue Amp Media exists.** Ellie spent weeks on this. Late nights, archived newspapers, property records, court filings, FBI interview transcripts -- cross-referencing details that a 13-year-old girl remembered 40 years ago against documents that the DOJ tried to keep hidden. And she found things. Verifiable, documented things. That is not nothing. That is exactly what independent journalism is supposed to do, and almost never does anymore. There are still 37 pages missing. This story is not over. And Ellie is not stopping. A paid subscription to Blue Amp Media directly supports this work -- and everything else we do to hold power accountable, keep the midterms alive, and make sure the people who need to answer for what they've done don't get to just walk away. If that matters to you, we'd be glad to have you with us. Subscribe below. And thank you for reading Ellie 's work. She's the real deal. -- Cliff Schecter, Blue Amp Media You're currently a free subscriber to . For the full experience, | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Cliff Schecter PO Box 8384, Cincinnati, OH 45208 ? ?

Friends — Trump's EPA just proposed weakening limits on emissions of a gas called ethylene oxide from manufacturing facilities across the country.
Ethylene oxide is used to sterilize medical equipment, but **long-term exposure is linked to leukemia, breast cancer, lymphoma, and other cancers.** The EPA itself classified it as a human carcinogen in 2016, finding it was 60 times more toxic to children than previously thought.
**Now, roughly 2.3 million people living near these facilities are put at even greater risk because of this inhumane rollback.**
These neighborhoods are disproportionately low-income communities and communities of color that have long shouldered the heaviest burden of industrial pollution in this country.
And make no mistake: This is part of a devastating and deliberate pattern. In recent months alone, Trump's EPA has weakened restrictions on mercury from coal-burning power plants and repealed the scientific finding that gave the government the legal authority to regulate climate pollution.
**So we must ask ourselves who benefits from these rollbacks? It’s certainly not everyday people. These attacks are designed to serve Big Industry and Big Oil — the same polluters that have spent decades profiting while communities pay the price.**
That’s exactly why the team here at JanePAC is working around the clock to elect leaders at every level of government who will fight for people, not profits. We're laser-focused on flipping the House this November and electing leaders with the courage to finally put a check on Trump’s dirty fossil fuel agenda.

Moves to Weaken Limits on a Cancer-Causing Gas | Friends — Trump's EPA just proposed weakening limits on emissions of a gas called ethylene oxide from manufacturing facilities across the country. Ethylene oxide is used to sterilize medical equipment, but long-term exposure is linked to leukemia, breast cancer, lymphoma, and other cancers. The EPA itself classified it as a human carcinogen in 2016, finding it was 60 times more toxic to children than previously thought. Now, roughly 2.3 million people living near these facilities are put at even greater risk because of this inhumane rollback. These neighborhoods are disproportionately low-income communities and communities of color that have long shouldered the heaviest burden of industrial pollution in this country. And make no mistake: This is part of a devastating and deliberate pattern. In recent months alone, Trump's EPA has weakened restrictions on mercury from coal-burning power plants and repealed the scientific finding that gave the government the legal authority to regulate climate pollution. So we must ask ourselves who benefits from these rollbacks? It’s certainly not everyday people. These attacks are designed to serve Big Industry and Big Oil — the same polluters that have spent decades profiting while communities pay the price. That’s exactly why the team here at JanePAC is working around the clock to elect leaders at every level of government who will fight for people, not profits. This is a monumental first step in this race, Peter, and I couldn’t have done it without each and every one of you. I turned in ballot petitions signed by thousands of grassroots supporters across New Mexico — a true testament to just how strong our grassroots campaign is — and how it's growing every single day.

But we can’t slow down now.

FIVE Republicans are running to bring Donald Trump’s extremist, fear-driven agenda here to New Mexico. Republicans know this is one of their best pick-up opportunities, and they're ready to pour MILLIONS to flip our state red.

But we won’t let them.

I’m ready to stop anyone who wants to drag us backward or divide our communities. I’ll move New Mexico forward. I’ll get our kids reading in kindergarten. I’ll bring the trades to middle schools for early on hands-on experience. I’ll make sure law enforcement has the tools they need to take violent criminals and illegal drugs off our streets. clean_body: This is a huge, and monumental first step in this race, Peter, and I couldn’t have done it without each and every one of you. | = = Hi Peter, Deb Haaland here with exciting news! I am officially on the ballot to be the next governor of New Mexico. = | = This is a monumental first step in this race, Peter, and I couldn’t have done it without each and every one of you. I turned in ballot petitions signed by thousands of grassroots supporters across New Mexico — a true testament to just how strong our grassroots campaign is — and how it's growing every single day. But we can’t slow down now. FIVE Republicans are running to bring Donald Trump’s extremist, fear-driven agenda here to New Mexico. Republicans know this is one of their best pick-up opportunities, and they're ready to pour MILLIONS to flip our state red. But we won’t let them. I’m ready to stop anyone who wants to drag us backward or divide our communities. I’ll move New Mexico forward. I’ll get our kids reading in kindergarten. I’ll bring the trades to middle schools for early on hands-on experience. I’ll make sure law enforcement has the tools they need to take violent criminals and illegal drugs off our streets. If you’re sick, you’ll see a doctor — without breaking the bank. Your rent won’t be set by AI. I’ll fight to get you the raise you deserve. And I will not let ICE terrorize our communities. In New Mexico, they will not be masked and will be held accountable. I will build a New Mexico where every single person is safe, healthy, and able to thrive. That’s why I will continue traveling the state meeting New Mexicans, rolling out my policy plans on affordability, public safety and health care, and demonstrating that I have the leadership, passion, and experience to be the next governor of New Mexico. Hi Peter,

I grew up in a home where lights, heat, and running water weren’t always guaranteed. By the time I graduated high school, my family had been evicted three times.

**When I say I’m running to make life more affordable for Wisconsin families, I mean it — this fight is personal to me.**

That’s why the centerpiece of my campaign is a real plan to make Wisconsin more affordable for working families. Here’s what it means:

**💼 Jobs and wages that build futures:** Good-paying, union-backed jobs — created block by block through a statewide expansion of my Building Bridges program.

**🏘️ Affordable, safe housing across Wisconsin:** Building and preserving housing in rural, suburban, and urban communities — with faster permitting and energy-efficient construction.

**🏥 Health care that reaches people:** Expanding mobile outreach, addiction treatment, and EMS innovations so care shows up when and where it's needed.

**⚡ Climate action that creates jobs:** Investing in solar, energy retrofits, and clean infrastructure — creating thousands of union jobs while lowering costs for families.

**🎒 Strong schools and early learning:** Universal early childhood education, new investments in public schools, and closing the special education reimbursement gap.

What sets me apart in this race is that these aren’t just talking points. In Milwaukee County, we’ve already delivered — investing more than $45 million in affordable housing, preventing thousands of evictions, and helping create over 40,000 new jobs. I know how to get results.

But running a campaign to put working families above ultra-wealthy donors takes resources. And right now, we’re in a critical stretch.

clean_body: Kat is the only leading candidate in the race who is willing to call what is happening in Gaza a genocide. | | | Friend, Together, we’re challenging the political status quo that puts billionaire and corporate power over everyday people. That’s why I am proud to endorse Kat Abughazaleh in tomorrow’s primary in Illinois’ 9th congressional district. Kat is the only leading candidate in the race who is willing to call what is happening in Gaza a genocide. As a 26-year-old Palestinian American, she represents a new generation of leadership. And as a renter, a formerly uninsured worker, and a union representative, Kat understands the struggles of working people. AIPAC is pouring millions of dollars into this race in an attempt to install another pro-genocide member of Congress. But Kat has a chance to beat AIPAC money with our grassroots support. She rejects corporate PAC money and billionaire Republican money. | Kat is a journalist and researcher who has taken on the far-right. She’s fighting to defend democracy, demand economic justice, and advance a humane U.S. foreign policy. Through her grassroots campaign, Kat is already serving her community―having her campaign office double as a mutual aid hub that collects and distributes toiletries, hygiene products, clothes, books, diapers, food, and more. Her policy proposals include expanding the child tax credit to reach more families, ensuring a basic minimum income for stay-at-home parents and caregivers, and guaranteeing at least a year of paid parental leave. | | Dear Fellow Conservative, You know it and I know it -- Congress is broken. Politicians have turned “serving the people” into “serving themselves.” They use their positions to get richer and richer every year, while you and I get left behind. Left-wing radicals like Ilhan Omar, Rashida Tlaib, and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez work to destroy our country from within. And Washington never fixes anything. **[Today, WE THE PEOPLE have a chance to do something about it when you sign your “Time for Term Limits” petition and submit it in the next 72 hours.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** Our Founding Fathers never intended for government service to be a permanent career. George Washington famously served just two terms — then went home. Our Founding Fathers also said our government was made for a “moral and religious people.” And they understood that if that moral compass broke down, Congress could easily steer America in the wrong direction, become a do-nothing body, or make government a gravy train for themselves. That’s why they included a powerful safeguard in our Constitution -- an escape hatch -- enshrined in Article V. If Congress ever became too corrupt to fix itself, Article V. says the states can use this provision in the Constitution to act. 34 state legislatures can call a convention, propose term limits -- and Congress can’t do a thing about it. [**Here at AMAC Action, we have led the term limits movement in the past, and we are ready to put our efforts behind the movement once again.**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
[ **Time for Term Limits** ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
My friend, can you imagine Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez spending 30 more years in Congress?? We are AMAC Action. “AMAC” stands for Association of Mature American Citizens. And when it comes to standing up for the rights of Americans, “action” is what we’re known for. President Trump has said that AMAC Action is so effective that members of Congress run the other way when they see our delegates coming down the hall. And our **“Time for Term Limits”** Petition Drive certainly has Washington lifers on the run! [**Please sign your petition and submit it in the next 72 hours.**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
**> > **No more golden pensions for people who work 170 days a year and spend half of that just trying to get reelected. **> > **No more using the power of the office to destroy American values from within. **> >** No more insider deals to get rich. **> >** No more jobs for life with nothing to show for it!
---
Some of these grifters and America-haters have been “working” in Congress over 30, and even 40 years!
---
* **Maxine Waters — 34 years**
* **Chuck Schumer — 44 years**
* **Patty Murray — 33 years**

---
They’ve been in the swamp so long they’ve grown gills. Please – let’s not let them drag America down into the swamp with them. It’s time to use the escape hatch our Founders left for us. 34 state legislatures are needed. What will embolden states to act is seeing a massive groundswell of support for term limits from millions of Americans just like you. That’s why AMAC Action is spearheading this massive 50-state Petition Drive and why you got my email today. You’ve proven that you’re a patriot who can be counted on to take action. **[Please sign your “Time for Term Limits” petition and submit it in the next 72 hours with your sacrificial donation of $35, $50 or more to spread this national campaign across America.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** We need to reach **1 million** patriots with petitions just like yours. And that takes time and money. The Washington lifers are counting on having more power, influence, and resources than the American people. They’re counting on our complacency and despair. But here at AMAC Action we say: Let’s finish the fight our Founders began and restore America’s government to the people. Your $35 gift is enough to send and collect 50 more **“Time for Term Limits”** petitions across email, text, and mail. Your gift of $70 funds 100 more **“Time for Term Limits”** petitions. Singlehandedly, you are an indispensable force-multiplier in this effort. But if you do nothing, nothing changes.
---
* Immigration policy will never get fixed and just stay a meaningless election year talking point.
* America’s spending and debt will continue to grow unchecked. Remember when we had a balanced budget? We can get back there if career politicians do something!
* Social Security will keep getting raided while real policies to protect your benefits sit on the back burner.
* Healthcare costs will do nothing but skyrocket leaving seniors vulnerable.
* America’s children will stay trapped in the leftwing indoctrination centers we call “public schools.”
* Radicals like Ilhan Omar, Corey Booker, and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez will continue to undermine America’s founding values.
* And the Washington, D.C. fat-cats will just get fatter and lazier.

---
Please join our army of patriots who are fed-up with the Washington lifers who work against our interests while our country sinks. What’s even more frustrating is that President Trump has policies that can save the ship and Washington lifers stand in his way! **[Your signed “Time for Term Limits” petition is critical. And we appreciate your donation whether it’s $35, $50 or anything higher or lower. What’s most important is that you respond in the next 72 hours.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** **One million “Time for Term Limits” petitions is a bold goal but we can do it if we all pitch in.** Every dollar helps. Every signature counts. Every day matters. Thank you and may God bless you and these United States.

**Rebecca Weber,_Chairwoman_** **AMAC Action**

subject: Why do you support Marie?
body:
| | Peter,

March is Women’s History Month, and here in Southwest Washington we’re proud to have a representative who’s helped break barriers.

Before coming to Congress, Marie ran an auto repair shop – one of the few women in the trades – and she’s brought that same independent, roll-up-your-sleeves mindset to the work she does for our communities every day.

**This month, we want to highlight the voices of the people who power this campaign: supporters like you. Would you be willing to record a short video telling us why you support Marie?**

It doesn’t need to be fancy, just a quick phone video is perfect. If you need a jumping off point, here are a few ideas:
* Why do you support Marie?

El Salvador marked its [first-ever appearance](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD2ypCAURleDmRZ_gxgQTGLWk05I3dYL3ikEC-m23P3U6-Bt4G3g-845fx_-AZQoxz-wowsx-BaKz3idCVvD6g-okO79IMhnpNAoxwNzfJGXXJqeq14YvwKl2-tudQFRourQiXFUZhJ6tN3muFHKWmGkWZ58nJ4iTEIYw-2irIVJdOS-1rgSRnKulRn0OFkhphCE5vALJdMcV2qlDv8K5bZhSHd5Yx2WsnfJba0dJ1O_mZyZnK_rGr65l6HUyOQcENqrIpPzTgly6ZdSG2XoPx6Y-hPSG9ZS-43OVurdVbceF6VEpxmZ5nEHSp-_9uNQbyf_BwAA__8hTH6I) at the 2026 Winter Paralympics with two unlikely trailblazers. David Chávez, 27, and Jonathan Arias, 28, competed in para cross-country skiing in Milan-Cortina, a remarkable achievement for athletes from a tropical country where most people have never seen snow. [Both men were paralyzed](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGvpSAUhH-NdhhABC0otrG7225pzpWDnruIBljN3V__4iteXv_KmUkm882fx_QAChSX37Ch9Yufit-niFcOWAqm6YAE4b0dBDEv5AvF5cC4_KNJcqkZb5nQkwMK70nVznpEiW2NVhjT6kEo09erFZ0y7qnRdBJ06_seOuN6JbSa516YZ032buOt0JJz1epGmaEXYvBeKA4dykpxdFT21Lx2imVFH977iamZ960Odi3lyFX7q5JjJcfrupr4nG-KO6_kmI89lVzJ8QtnvtVFsWBi30zm4CTH5hVO_M9ee4SyQmSQCDLLf4niwtIcQXbDMKg6WXdcFAJlbSrFlw0ofE4qP_7ytPIjAAD__6mWjH8) in separate gang shootings at age 14, injuries that once left them unsure what their futures might hold. They eventually found a new path through adaptive sports, first meeting through wheelchair basketball before discovering elite competition. With help from American coaches and supporters, the pair turned to cross-country skiing. They trained in creative ways back home, including pushing their ski equipment through thick beach sand to build strength before competing overseas. They hope their journey shows other Salvadorans with disabilities that even after devastating setbacks, new possibilities are still within reach. ## Wife's iPhone Hunch Saves Husband
A Washington skier survived more than four hours buried under an avalanche at Stevens Pass last month [after his wife tracked him](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL3OnDAQAJ8Guj35hzO4cJHmukubEi14DRsZ2wJziLePLq_w1SONRvPnPb6RI6flN27kwhLGGvKY6Doi1Ur7WHDHeG-FMR0Lh8ppKZSWk0cllAGhQZrRI8d77FrvApEi3ZKTfa-NlV0_tKuTdkBrJBk_6eegA6EZBvUUZg5azWhbdl-b0NIoITptHl1vByltCLIT-CTVdII817w__mZOdaUQ7_yh_THnrY1urbUcjf7VqFejXoVyifRFjXpdHAjOgzwETh62G7isORHUDDHPWAnW85gwebjWDBceMJ07k4fpBvxgxDSvBFJaaY3U7e58uThGPkzfdGLZkOP_ivrjfR-n_gUAAP__D7uGdA) using Apple's Find My iPhone and directed ski patrol to his precise location. Michael Harris was making his final run of the day through Big Chief Bowl when a slab gave way, sweeping him into a snow hole where [debris pinned him beneath](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO3CAUAL8Gd6wAc3AuKNK4u7QprbfmYb8EAwJsZ_8-2vzC9aPRaH59LV9AkdL2Ew50YQtLD3lJeLeIvWNdClSIr6MQpLZR6JS2gmk7aVFCGS5GLs3igeJr0YN3AVHhOKCT1o5mktp-DruTCryRWtgnBpThKcW0CutByFUY-_EcyL1tYpRGCaFH89B2-pRyCkFqAR-omBboqef6-J0p9R1DfOUL62PNxxDd3ntpbPzB1MzUfN_3I5-9kcecIiV8U0zN-ew-58rBX5j6WZGpGf-WmCt0yom3s150QWRqPmjdASPfoVZqnMqeE3Iohbc_xNQ8VOfLTTFSM5ZpsR1A8X9M__bFy6l_AQAA__9Ecotw) what he described as snow that felt like cement. His wife, Penny, had a gut feeling something was wrong, checked the app, and noticed his location hadn't moved in hours, so she contacted Stevens Pass ski patrol and handed them a live GPS snapshot from her phone before driving to the mountain herself. Avalanche experts say survival odds drop sharply after just 15 minutes of burial, and [nearly no one survives](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGSpCAURb9GMyxARAwINjHrTTek3jYPfbsIlDBa_fdTPfMJE9-qe-qcPw_3AIqUtt9woA1bcC1kl_CuEVvD0xU4Ib6OQpDqRqFR2gqm7YOc5FIzPjKhnQeKL6d6bwOixLFHK-Z51ItQs-l3qw1f_ko1yacCMH4ywsO4TEoHg-DN0pN9v_FRaMm5GvWg5sUIsYQgFIcJZac4emr5HP5lSm3HEF_5wnN45qOPdm-t1G781cm1k-t930PJt_-eO7m-fTq5UtlzQlbhQs_qf8KzskgBGVwQIT13ZLXhhamyArX2p_Xlphip6rlTfDuA4hew_bjUZeVnAAAA___hoYCF) past two hours, making Harris's four-hour ordeal a statistical near-impossibility. Rescuers dug him out, conscious but severely hypothermic, with a body temperature in the 70s; hospital staff [nicknamed him Miracle Avalanche Man](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DHO4yAUBODT4M4RPLCJC4pt3GXbLRGOH_htMFhAYuX2K-8V_maq0XzS_HnYh6NIKfx2OxofvG0-24RnjdgaFnu44uJ3P8ilGsg3SuHAFN5kgcPYc9mL0a6O4teqbjUeEVB2aITWcpyE0vduMwP3KAcvuNTDMK4Dh0UALjBNoJdlwI7MtcalGIFzJceb0tNdiMl7obgbEJjiuFLL5fY3U2ob-vjNHyy3Z967aLbWjsrkLwYzg_mdsvf0JBcTtjOXV71qDOYLYTBzeYViMNcXYelVv-V3qb37uOjSc8P-dHWjFFpODOaumPU4KUaqo2aKh91R_A-3Hz_2MfAvAAD__zO6gEc), and Harris put it simply: _"She's my lifesaver."_

Live Nation and Ticketmaster rigged the system — and you've been paying for it.
If you've ever tried to buy tickets to a concert or sporting event on Ticketmaster, you know how frustrating the system can be.
That’s on purpose — and it’s why I filed a landmark antitrust lawsuit against Live Nation, the parent company of Ticketmaster, back in 2024.
They've been using their dominance in ticketing and live events to squeeze out competitors and drive up prices for fans, harming consumers and the entire live music industry.
A week into the trial, the U.S. Department of Justice announced it was abandoning this lawsuit and settling with Live Nation.
Well, California won’t take the lackluster deal.
Today, we’re heading back to trial without the Feds to hold Live Nation accountable and get a better deal for the American people.
Allowing big corporations to illegally create monopolies so they can rake in cash will only worsen the affordability crisis here in California and across the country. And as your Attorney General, I won’t stand by while that happens.
Holding those who abuse their power accountable is my job, and I’m going to get it done.
But taking on powerful corporations requires resources and staying power, so I need you on my team.

The National Mall—sacred ground for Let Us Worship!

For six years, God has opened the door for us to lift up praise and worship right in the heart of our nation’s capital. By His grace, we’re headed back again—with a big announcement.

In the middle of the historic United States Semiquincentennial celebrations, God has opened wide a door for us to return for the seventh year in a row.

# [Tell Trump: "Stop Disrespecting the Troops"](https://default.salsalabs.org/T5f1be88a-3291-43e1-9a1c-907d4b027b02/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)

---
| | | President Trump has been disrespecting our troops for years ("suckers and losers", mocking a Gold Star family, etc.), so it's not too suprising that he's still doing it now. But we're now in the middle of a war, and many of them are getting killed and wounded, so it really would be great if Trump could show even the tiniest bit of class and respect, and avoid doing things like:
* Wearing a crappy [baseball ](https://default.salsalabs.org/T6a8fea64-0cb5-452a-8f5e-4528f32b564c/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)[cap](https://default.salsalabs.org/T62547c0f-6bc9-43e7-8a25-3da547415bdf/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9) to a dignified transfer of fallen troops -- and then selling the same caps online to make money.
* Using another ceremony commemorating fallen soldiers to brag about [his ](https://default.salsalabs.org/T0a275d54-d45a-4a05-95df-2955c7deec25/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)[drapes](https://default.salsalabs.org/T28eb6de8-3765-44bb-9914-b644ef2ca218/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9).
* Calling the Iran war an "excursion", as if it were a picnic in the forrest.

And most disrespectful of all -- sending troops to risk their lives in a war that was unnecessary, and that Trump can't even come up with a straight reason for. It's hard to get worse than that. [**Please add your name: "President Trump, stop disrespecting the troops."**](https://default.salsalabs.org/T50d3e2fe-afe3-4d4e-be5c-a399e02ee540/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)
